title: Leningrad
description: Designed by Dick Rustin.  Artists:  Chris Dickson, Rodger B. MacGowan, Lise Patterson, Redmond Askel Simonsen and Alan Wykes.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  The Advance of Army Group North, Summer 1941. BGG and DG for further information!

title: Les Chevaliers de la Table Ronde - en français
description:
Designed by Bruno Cathala & Julien Delval.  As arted by Cyrille Daujean & Julien Delval.  In English: Shadows over Camelot.
A highly recommended game:
2006 Spiel des Jahres "Fantasy Game" Winner; 2006 Golden Geek Best Light / Party Game Nominee; 2006 Golden Geek Best Gamer's Board Game Nominee; 2006 As d'Or - Jeu de l'Année Nominee; 2005 Tric Trac Nominee; 2005 Spiel der Spiele Hit für Experten Recommended; 2005 Spiel der Spiele Hit für Experten Recommended; 2005 Origins Awards Gamer’s Choice Best Board Game of the Year Winner; 2005 Meeples' Choice Award; 2005 Japan Boardgame Prize Best Advanced Game Winner; 2005 International Gamers Awards - General Strategy; Multi-player Nominee.
notes: Conversion by Unknown. Shadows over Camelot is a cooperative/semi-cooperative hand-management and deduction-based board game for 3–7 players. Anonymous found and sent this older ZT1 title - not on our Green List! Bsed on our research, this is a game which needs to be played!  Very highly regarded, based on it's awards! See BGG and Days of Wonder for more information!

title: Les Maréchaux (The Marshals) - In French
description:
Designed by Denis Sauvage.  Art by Christophe Camilotte and Pascal da Silva.  3 games are included:
Dupont's; Victor's and Suchet's campaigns.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Les Maréchaux (The Marshals) is an operational wargame designated to simulate campaigns led by French marshals and generals of French Revolution and 1st Empire, when Napoleon was not directly acting on the theater of operations. See BGG and Vae Victis for rules and more information!

title: Les Quatre-Bras & Waterloo 1815 PLUS
description:
Designed by Frédéric Bey. Arted by Pascal da Silva.
As first seen in Jours De Gloire #39 & #40 . . . This is a ZIP file, please download and then extract the contents.  This will give you access to ZTB and included PDF.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Les Quatre-Bras and Waterloo 1815 is a complete game in the Jours de Gloire series. It covers the battles which occurred on June 16th and 18th, during Napoléon’s offensive in Belgium against the armies of Wellington and Blücher. See BGG , Jours de gloire and ludifolie for more information!

title: Leuthen PLUS
description:
Designed by T. Gordon. Graphics by T. Gordon.
This DIY project began about 30 years ago, and the hand-drawn map dates from that period. The current counter images were created in 2015 using Vassal. Most of the charts and tables were devised at that time. As this is a one-man project, it would be fair to assume that it has not been adequately play-tested.
Please leave a message on ZT Forums with your playtests.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. An original game concerning the 1757, Battle of Leuthen. Historically this was Frederick II greatest victory (of Prussia). ZT Folk, we have no BGG information.  Because this is an original design. This is a ZIP file, please un-zip to get to ZTB & Rules! Complements of Mr. Gordon!!

title: Leuthen v1.0
description:
Designed by Frank Chadwick.  As arted by Tim Allen.
Many thanks to VPG for allowing this module to be made freely available.
ZT Folk:  we believe this was an old ZT1 box - as found by 'Unknown Soldier" - Thank you sir!
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett. Frederick's Greatest Victory  5 December, 1757! "Leuthen is the first game in the Drums & Muskets series - a new system that recreates battles of the 18th Century, from roughly the adoption of the socket bayonet through the French Revolution." See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Leuthen: Frederick's Greatest Victory
description:
Designed by Paul Dangel. Counter graphics by Paul Dangel. Map Graphics by Rick Barber.
Awards:   1997 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargaming Graphics Nominee; 1997 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  I haved added markers to make it possible to use the casualty rosters on screen. Full historical setup provided. Leuthen (Battles from the Age of Reason, Vol. 3) presents both gamers and students of the period with a colorful and meticulously detailed simulation with which to explore the actual events and possibilities of this definitive battle. See BGG and COA (Clash of Arms Games)for more information.

title: Libertadores 1810-1824
description: Designed by Enric Marti. Graphics by Javier Romero and Xavier P. Rotllán. Originally published in Soldados y Estrategia, vol. 2 no. 10.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in Spanish and English. Includes scenario setups for all ten battles. (Note that all of the maps are on one tab.) See BGG and Ludopress for more information!

title: Liberty Roads v1.0
description:
The D-Day Landings and Campaign in France 1944-45
Designed by Yves Le Quellec and Nicolas Rident
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett. Contains three scenarios (D-Day/Campaign, Market-Garden and Cobra) as well as multiple game ones. There are both English and French versions, but it loads the English D-Day/Campaign scenario by default. See BGG and Hexasim for further information!

title: Ligny and Wavre 1815
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey. Arted by Pascal da Silva.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Ligny and Wavre 1815 is a complete game in the Jours de Gloire series. It covers the battles which occurred on June 16th, 18th and 19th, during Napoléon’s offensive in Belgium against the armies of Wellington and Blücher. See BGG , Jours de gloire and ludifolie for more information!

links.url: https://zuntzu.com/gameboxes/Canon en Carton/1815 JdG Ligny Wavre.ztb

title: Like Lions They Fought
description:
Designed by Dennis L. Bishop.  Sometime artists are not attributed.  Should you know, please note this on ZT Forums.
As seen in Command Magazine #28.
notes: Conversion by S Rugge.  Simulation of the Anglo-Zulu War. Game starts with a chance for the Zulus to maul the Brits who are exposed. After that, the Brits need to capture Zulu Kraals (burn 'em down) and capture Cetshwayo to win. Zulus win by avoiding the British victory conditions. See BGG for more information!

title: Lille
description: Designed by Brent Nosworthy and David Werden.  Artist Unknown.  During this period, artists were not always attributed? Part of the Art of Siege quad.  ZT Note:  This is the third game to be uploaded using 'Submission Button.'
notes: Conversion by maxfin.  The Classic Vauban Siege, 1708. the greatest star fortress in France is taken by the Anglo-Dutch-German Confederation. See BGG & DG for further information!

title: Lilliburlero: The Battle of Boyne, July 1690
description: Designed by Phillip Jelley, Lembet Tohver and art by Mark Mahaffey.  As seen in ATO Magazine #40.
notes: Conversion by David Jones.  Historical Battle that went from Pike's & Muskets to the new technology of Flint-lock warfare a time where Cavalry caracole competed a charge!  See BGG and ATO for further information!

title: Line of Battle (2nd Edition)
description: Designed by Stephen Newberg (of SimCan).  Omega graphics by Nicolás Eskubi and Adrian George.  With permission by Omega Games and Stephen Newberg.
notes: Conversion by David L. Jones.  Reimplements SimCan's  (1986) game "Line of Battle."   For Naval fans, well worth the review and play.  An interesting set of rules for prospective designers! See BGG and Omega Games for further information (sorry, no link? - please inform).

title: Lion of Ethiopia
description:
Designed by Michael Duffeld.  Graphics by Mark Simonitch.
Awards: 1990 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee.
As first seen in Command Magazine #4.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.   As published in Command Magazine #4.  This game covers the Italian Campaign to conquer Ethiopia in 1935-36.  Game box includes setup for basic game, and also extra counters published in Command Magazines #7 and #8. See BGG for more information!

title: Little War (2 of 2)
description: Designed by Brian Train.  Artists:  Jose Ramon Faura & Amabel Holland.  Part of a two-game package.  See Ukraine Crisis 2.0 on this site.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson. Prolific designer Brian Train (The Scheldt Campaign) has created a number of games on unusual, under-gamed topics, often utilizing unique and innovative mechanisms. Hollandspiele is proud to be bringing two of Mr. Train's most interesting designs to your table in a single box. The Little War is a smaller game about a smaller conflict: the week-long 1939 border war between Hungary and Slovakia. See BGG , Hollandspiele and Wargame Vault for further information!

title: Lobositz, Battle of
description: Designed by Frank Chadwick.  Artwork by Steve Banner.  Republished in Command Magazine Japan #45 in 2002, along with 1941: Operation Barbarossa.
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  A series 120 game concerning Fredrick the Great - - an excellent game of the Seven Years War.  Very few games on this subject. See BGG and FarFutures for further information!

title: Lonato
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey.  As arted by Pascal Da Silva & Rodger B. MacGowan.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Lonato is a self-contained module covering the battles of Lonato, July 31 - August 4, 1796, using the downloadable rules for the Triumph and Glory (T&G) system, part of GMT Games' "Gameplayer's Series" which has playability as its main objective. See BGG and RBM Studios for more information.

title: Lost Cities
description:
Designed by Reiner Knizia.  Artists (all versions):  Vincent Dutrait, Michaela Kienle, Anke Pohl, Thilo Rick, Claus Stephan and Franz Vohwinkel.
Awards:  2019/Fall Parents' Choice Gold Award Winner.  2006 Juego del Año Winner. 2006 Juego del Año Finalist. 2004 Gra Roku Game of the Year Nominee.  2000 International Gamers Awards - General Strategy; Two-players.  1999 Meeples' Choice Award.  1999 Fairplay À la carte Runner-up!!!!!!
notes: Conversion by MAZ.  For the daring and adventurous, there are too many lost cities to seek and explore. You must own the game to download it. See BGG and KOSMOS for further information!

title: Luftwaffe:  Aerial Combat - Germany 1943 to 1945
description: Designed by Joseph Miranda and Louis Zocchi.  As arted by Nicolás Eskubi  & Joseph Youst.
notes: Conversion by S Rugge.  This version of Luftwaffe is a remake of the Avalon Hill classic.  Concerning the Allied strategic air-war against NAZI Germany. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Maciejowice 1794
description:
Designed by Adam Niechwiej. Counters by Jacek Grzesiowski.
Gentle-Folks, an excellent game which gives historic understanding of Polish resistance.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Maciejowice 1794 depicts the last battle of Thaddeus Kosciuszko. Poles were opposed by a Russian Army led by General Ivan Fersen. Charts in English. See BGG and Strategemata for more information!

title: Mad Anthony:  War for Ohio 1791-94
description: Designed by Joseph Miranda.  Originally arted by Nicolás Eskubi  (including counters).  As first seen in S&T magazine #242.
notes: Conversion by S Rugge. In this game, each turn represents between one week and one month, depending on the time of year, and each hexagon on the map represents 10 miles across. Units of maneuver for the US Army are primarily battalions, while Indian units are warbands, awarded one strength point for each 80 to 120 individuals within them.  Low complexity, 280 counters. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Mage Knight -- Po Polsku
description:
Designed by Kevin Barrett and Jordan Weisman.  Graphics by 13+ artists, please see BGG listing.
We are unsure of Publisher; please leave a message on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by Sirafin.  Mage Knight cleverly applies the CCG concept to miniatures; a "Starter Pack" contains 10 random pre-painted, plastic miniatures, while "Booster Packs" contain 5. Figures' stats are kept track of via dials on their bases, which change depending on how much damage they've taken. As in most miniatures games, players each create an army with the same number of points (with each miniature having a different point value), then take turns moving and attacking until all of the opponent's forces are dead or captured, the opponent withdraws, or your pre-determined time limit expires. See BGG and WizKids for more information!

title: Magenta 1859 Deluxe
description:
By Luc Olivier, Philippe Klarmann, Nicolas Zamichiei, Riccardo Rinaldi.
Insert of VaeVictis #73, By kind permission of Histoire & Collections.
notes: Conversion by Jerome.  The Battle of Magenta, June 4, 1859, was the first major clash between France and Austria during the Second Italian War of Independence. See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for further information!

title: Magic Realm
description: Designed by Richard Hamblen.  Original artwork by Richard Hamblen, George Goebel, Kim Grommel, Randall C. Reed and Chris White.
notes: Conversion by Anonymous.  Should you know ZTB Author, please leave a post on ZT Forums. Fantasy adventuring, set in a land filled with monsters.  I created this gamebox to test ZunTzu capabilities  Game Documentation/Rules (PDF) are not included. See BGG and Avalon Hill (worldwide) for more information! NOTE:  Well done!

title: Magnificent (气壮山河) (in Chinese & English))
description:
Anti-Japanese War Campaign Quadrigame (3rd edition). Designed by Bai Yuhao.
ZT NOTE:  This is our FIRST Chinese ZTB and #918th ZTB!!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English and Chinese (note that the English-language charts on the map are terrain pieces that can be removed to reveal the original Chinese versions). This is a quad game of the 2nd Sino-Japanese War. It consists of the following four games. 1) Third Battle of Changsha 2) Battle of the Great Wall 3) Battle of West Hubei 4) Hundred Regiments OffensiveSetups provided for all games and scenarios (including the bonus fifth game). See BGG & Face Book (?) for more information.

title: Maida - 4 juillet 1806
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey.  As arted by Pascal Da Silva.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. The 14th and 15th battle of the Jours de Gloire series, this one's a DTP effort from Canons en Carton. See BGG , Vae Victis and Cannon en Carton for more information!

title: Malaya & Burma (日本の進撃) - English & Japanese
description: Designed by Ishikawa Akira.  Artwork by Rodger B. MacGowan (?).
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  Not two as the title suggests, but three separate games in one box: Race to Singapore covers the Malaya Campaign in 1941-1942, Burma the Japanese invasion of that country at a similar scale, and Fall of Singapore is a tactical/low level operational game about the Japanese assault on the island of Singapore itself. There are "rough" linking rules to join the two campaign scenarios. Charts in English and Japanese. Setups (with basic air units) provided for all three games. See BGG and Hobby Japan for more information.

title: Mallorca
description: Designed by Javier Hoyos. Part of the series Guerra Civil Española.  As first seen in Ludopress' Alea No. 24.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English and Spanish, including series charts from No Pasaran. Setup provided for Scenario 1. This is a scenario for the ¡No Pasaran!: Las Batallas por Madrid 1936-37 system for the Spanish Civil War. It requires the use of the ¡No Pasaran! - Las Batallas por Madrid for rules. This is not a stand alone game although it has its own set of scenario-specific rules as well. For more info, see BGG and Alea-Ludopress !

title: Manassas
description:
2nd edition. Designed by Richard H. Britton. Graphics by Richard H. Britton and Leonard "Swamp" Cook. Published by Iron Crown Enterprises.
Awards: 1981 Charles S. Roberts Best Initial Release Nominee
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. For more info, see BGG and Iron Crown ! Tactical game of the First Battle of Manassas (Bull Run), 1861. It's a big, sprawling game that gives a great tactical feel for the battle. The ZTB adds three enhancements to the published game: * Hex numbers. * Larger, more readable elevation numbers on the map. * "X" markers to make it possible to track losses onscreen.

title: Manassas, 1st Battle of Bull Run (2nd GDW Edition)
description: Designed by: Tom Ellar & famed artist Roger B. MacGowen.  Awards:  1974 Charles S. Roberts Best Amateur Game Winner & 1974 Charles S. Roberts Best Amateur Game Nominee!
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  One of the first games concerning this battle.  A must play if you are a designer.  Many future civil war games built their ideas on Manassas! Few physical games exist . . . to see this historic wargame - - download this ZTB! See BGG and FarFutures.net for more information!

title: Manassas, 1st Edition (Historical Simulations Edition)
description:
Designed by Tom Eller. Artist Unknown: Original edition of the game republished by GDW in 1975.
Awards:  1974 Charles S. Roberts Best Amateur Game Winner and 1974 Charles S. Roberts Best Amateur Game Nominee.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. One of the earliest renditions on the 1st Bull Run in the American Civil War.  A must see for Civil War designers.  This is the first design and artisticaly different fron GDW's version!  Should you know the artist - - please respond on ZT Forums! See BGG and GDW's Far Futures for more information!

title: Marengo 1800
description:
Designed by Frédéric Bey.  Arted by Didier Bourgeois, Christophe Camilotte and Giuseppe Rava.  As first seen in VV magazine No. 35.
Awards:  2000 Charles S. Roberts Best Magazine-Published Boardgame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. This game covers the 1800 battle of Marengo, one of Napoleon's earliest great victories (when he was still merely "General Bonaparte") using a simplified version of the rules used in some of Vae Victis's other "Jours de Gloire" battle games (not to be confused with the rules used in the "Jours de Gloire: Campagne" series). See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for rules anf more information!

title: Marengo: Napoleon in Italy, 14 June 1800
description: Designed by David C. Isby, the famed military author.  Originally arted by Redmond Askel Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  One on four games included in the Napoleon At War QuadriGame.  "Marengo" is an operational level simulation of the battle between Napoleon's French Army and the Austrian Army commanded by General von Melas, which occurred on June 14, 1800 in Piedmont (northern Italy). See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Marita-Merkur: The Campaign in the Balkans, 1940 - 1941
description:
Designed by John Astell & Rich Banner.  Artist:  During this period of our wargame history, artists were not always attributed (should you know, please comment on ZT Forums).
This is a faithful rendition of this historical game!
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  Marita-Merkur, Europa III, recreates the campaign in the Balkans from November 1940 until June 1941.  Marita-Merkur is designed to be played by itself as a separate game, and also to mate with other Europa games.  This version includes the infamous 'orange' Greek Army.  Also see an updated version named "Balkan Front." See BGG , Europa Series Wargames (ESW), HMS/GRD and FarFutures.net for further information!

title: Marlborough at Blenheim
description: Designed by Daniel Scott Palter.  During this time, artists were not always attributed.  Should you know, please post on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Game of the Battle of Blenheim, Marlborough's famous victory of 1704 during the War of the Spanish Succession. See BGG and modern West End Games for more information!

title: Marston Moor
description: Designed by Bob Pollard. Published in issue 7 of The Wargamer.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  "Marston Moor" is a wargame simulation of the largest battle of the English Civil War. Fought in the county of Yorkshire, this battle decided the fate of the North and influenced the ultimate course of the war. See BGG for more information.

title: Mayday, 1st Edition
description: Designed by the famous Marc W. Miller.  As arted  (all editions) by David R. Deitrick, Naoyuki Kato and Rodger B. MacGowan.  Awards:  1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Fantasy / Futuristic Board Game Winner and 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Fantasy / Futuristic Board Game Nominee!
notes: Designed by R Peterson.  An award winning, series 120 game, which uses vector movement and is the 1st game to aide Traveller RPG players.  Playable under 2 hours. See BGG and FarFutures for further information (rules & more)!

title: Meatgrinder: the battle of Xuan Loc 1975
description:
Designed by Perry Moore, art by Mark Mahaffey.
As first seen in Against the Odds Magazine #33.  With permission by ATO.
notes: Conversion by Dave Jones.  Two years after the last US troops left Vietnam, People's Army of Vietnam (PAVN) General Van Tien Dung launched Operation 275, a "limited" offensive designed to set up an attack on the provincial capital of Pleiko. Rapid collapse of South Vietnamese (ARVN) forces caused a change in plan, with PAVN forces quickly taking one city after another, pausing only before an attack on Saigon itself. See BGG and ATO for further information!

title: Mecca
description: Designed by Javier García.  As arted by Chechu Nieto.
notes: Conversion by lianji.  A game of crowd management during Hajj.  Can you manage these millions of faithful? In a Muslim's pillar of faith? See BGG for more information!

title: Medellín 1809
description: Designed by José Antonio Vargas-Zúñiga. Map and counters by Sebas & Karles Autoedició. Published in issue 16 of Alea.   Part of La Sombra del Aguila series (Shadow of the Eagles).
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English and Spanish.  Shadow of the Eagle (La Sombra del Aguila) is a series of games covering the battles of the Napoleonic Wars in Spain (1808-1814). See BGG & Alea- Ludopress (Alea Magazine) for more information.

title: Medina de Rioseco 1808
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey.  Arted by Didier Bourgeois, Christophe Camilotte and Giuseppe Rava.  As first seen in VV magazine No. 83.  This game belongs to the Jours de Gloire series; based on a system by R. Berg.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Medina de Rioseco 1808 covers the battle of the 14 July 1808 between French army of marshal Bessières and the two Spanish armies of lieutnant-generals La Cuesta and Blake. See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for rules and more!

title: Men of Iron - Wakefield
description:
Designed by Richard H. Berg.  Artists: Rodger B. MacGowan Copyright 2018; Map: Knut Grunitz; Counters: Mike Lemick, Mark Simonitch, Charlie Kibler & Rodger B. MacGowan.
This game appeared in C3I magazine, number 31.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge. The Battle of Wakefield, 1460: It was at Wakefield that Richard, Duke of York, met his doom. Richard was head of the Yorkist faction, and had begun the rebellion against King Henry VI that is now known as the War of the Roses. It isn’t clear why he rode our that day against an army with numerical superiority, but the end result was calamity for the Yorkist contingent. About half the army perished, including Richard and the Earl of Salisbury (father of Warwick the kingmaker). Can you break the Lancastrian army before its reinforcements arrive or will you share Richard’s fate? Want to Play? Players Required: 1-2 Playing Time: 1-2 hours See C3I Magazine for more information!

title: Mercenary Air Squadron 1.1
description: Designed by Charlie Lewis and Jay Waschak.  Graphics by unknown, if you know, please leave a post on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by Keith Tracton.  As the year 2015 came to a close it was clear the world was in a new trend. Instead of fighting wars with their own conventional forces, nations found it easier to pass the burden of conflict along to private contractors. They could be expensive, but a mercenary force was less politically liable than a country and more expendable. The best survived, and went on to glory and profit. The most famous and sought after are the mercenary pilots. See BGG and VBAM Games for more information! An older ZTB found in the Geralt Collection. Submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Merchant of Venus 1st Edition
description: Designed by Richard Hamblen.  Graphics by Charles J. Kibler II, George Ira Parrish, Jr. and Regina DeSimone.
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  Merchant of Venus makes players take on the roles of space traders chasing wealth and fortune. Each player moves their ship through interconnected systems on a fixed map, discovering new alien worlds to trade with. As players start to make money delivering commodities, their earnings can be used to purchase equipment and construct their own infrastructure. The player who first acquires enough total value in cash and port/factory deeds wins the game. See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information! Found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by E. Sprauge.

title: Midway Solitaire
description:
Designed by Eric R. Harvey and Joseph Miranda.
Artists: Tom Willcockson and Joseph Youst.
As first seen in World at War Magazine #54.
Campaign in PTO in April-June 1942
notes: Conversion by Maaaax.  Set-up. This ztb does not contain rules. See BGG and Decision Games for more information!

title: Midway, 1964 V2.1 for ZT 3.17 PLUS
description: Designed by Larry Pinsk & Lindsley.  Classic game played by millions of players.  Third exemplar in demonstrating Block Game design in ZT! Latest update: 10/01/2022!
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan.   This gamebox optimizes Midway for ZunTzu (3rd Exemplar). It uses a third search board and the powerful features of ZunTzu to give TRUE DOUBLE-BLIND PLAY. You don't give away your position by calling out grid coordinates. Instead, ships' positions are marked in secret and revealed only when a search is conducted in that same area. (Yes, you NEED to play against an HONEST opponent!)  The Battle Board opens with the necessary CRT's, hit record pad, and break down counters. Even the tab layout aids the flow of play. Rules and specialized ZunTzu instructions included.  See BGG and Avalon Hill for further game information!  A useful game which leverages ZT3.17!!!

title: Midway, GDW version PLUS
description: Designer:  Marc W. Miller.  Artist, Rodger B. MacGowan.  Game designers: a must see for OBs of this classic Naval battle.  This version is not setup because of the complexity of historical submarines.  See ZIP file for more information.
notes: Conversion by R. Petereson.  Battle for Midway is a large scale air-naval simulation of the naval action between Japanese forces attempting to invade and seize Midway Island, and the American air, naval and land forces dedicated to holding it at all costs. This is a 120 MB ZIP file:  please download and unzip for ZTB and extras! See BGG and FarFutures for more information!

title: Midway: 1964 PLUS
description: Designed by Lawrence Pinsky and Lindsey Schutz.  During this era, artists were not always attributed!  Awards: Produced before any wargame awards like Charles S. Roberts Awards.  However, played by MULTITUDES of Grognard wargamers!
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  This version is fully playable via the ZT interface.  This is the 2nd 'exemplar' (see Cats Vs Dogs for first) in dealing with Block Games in ZT Design.  This is a ZIP file; please download and open for ZTB and other information! See BGG and modern Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Midway: The Battle of Midway 1942 AD
description: Designed by Paul Rohrbaugh. Graphics by Ilya Kudriashov, Terry Leeds and Mark Mahaffey.  With expressed permission of Steve Rawlings and TPS.
notes: Conversion by D. Jones. Midway is the decisive battle of the Pacific War. All agree that this one changed everything,  Explore this battle with this game! See BGG and TPS for more information!

title: Mighty Fortress, A, Reformation and Counter-Reformation, 1532-1555
description: Designed by Rudolph W. Heinze.  Arted by Nicolás Eskubi and Redmond Askel Simonsen.  Awards: In 1977, inducted into the Hall of Fame of the Charles S. Roberts Awards at Origins '78.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  A Mighty Fortress simulates the conditions, which made possible the spread of the Lutheran Reformation and the subsequent Catholic reaction (the Counter-Reformation) in the years 1532-1555. The game recreates the actual historical objectives of the major countries in Europe in the Sixteenth Century as well as their military strengths and resources. There are six players in the game representing the six major countries, England, France, the Ottoman Empire, the Hapsburgs, the Pope, and the collection of German states we will call The Lutherans. See BGG and DG for more information.

title: Mississippi Fortress
description: Designed by Gary Selkirk. Original graphics by Richard N. Barber and Mort Künstler.  Awards:  1990 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee - - need to see!
notes: Conversion by S Rugge.  'Mississippi Fortress' is the fifth game in CoA's Civil War Campaigns series. The game is a two player strategic simulation of General Ulysses S. Grant's campaign of 29 April through 4 July 1863 that culminated in the capture of the capture of Vicksburg and the splitting of the Confederacy. See BGG and Clash of Arms Games - COA for more information!

title: Mława 1939
description: 3rd (boxed) edition. Designed by Wojciech Zalewski and Szymon Kucharski. Map by Szymon Kucharski and Pior Prominski. Part of the Wrzesień 1939 series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. The battle for Mlawa was the first of many battles that occurred in the Northern Mazowsze in 1939 (Polish territory north of Warsaw). Here the German 3rd Army, commanded by General Kuchler, fought against the Polish Army "Modlin". Charts in Polish and English (the latter from the translated W39 system rulebook included in Kock 1939). Setup provided for the campaign scenario. See BGG & Taktyka i Strategia for more information.

title: Monmouth
description:
Designer: Richard Kane
Artists: Terry Leeds, Emanuel Gottleib Lutze, Timothy Schleif
notes: Conversion by Mitch King This game is Volume VI of the Battles of the Age of Reason series.  It explores Washington's attack on General Howe's rearguard as Howe retreats from Philadelphia for the safety of New York in June, 1778.  On the 28th, the Advanced Guard, under Charles Lee, bungles the attack and Washington is forced to come to Lee's rescue.  This is the first battle for the American army since leaving Valley Forge, where they trained extensively that spring under Baron von Steuben to fight toe-to-toe with British Regulars.  This game box contains setups for four scenarios. See BGG and Clash of Arms for more information.  One Player must own a copy of Monmouth in order to use this game box.  This game box posted with the kind permission of Ed Wimble.

title: Montebello NBS v1.0
description: Designed by François Vander Meulen, (Dean N. Essig, David A. Powell).  Graphics: Unknown.
notes: Conversion by Ichibrothers.  Free NBS (Napoleonic Brigade Series) game.  Montebello" is a complete free wargame meant to be an introduction to the Napoleonic Brigade Series (NBS). Its counter mix is small, and the full game can be played in a couple of hours. It depicts the battle of Montebello, June 9th, 1800. See BGG and MMP for further information!

title: Montenotte 1796 - In French
description: Designed by Vincent Gerard.  As arted by Pascal da Silva and René Théodore Berthon.  As originally seen in VV No.128.
notes: Conversion by the great L. Gary. Montenotte 1796 est le premier jeu d'une nouvelle série consacrée aux campagnes de l'époque révolutionnaire et impériale : La Grande Tactique. See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for more information!

title: Montmirail and Vauchamps 1814
description: Designed by the famed Frédéric Bey.  As arted by the equally famous Pascal Da Silva.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Montmirail and Vauchamps 1814 is a complete game in the Jours de Gloire series. It covers the battles which occurred on February 11 and 14, 1814, during Napoléon’s offensive against Blücher’s Army of Silesia. See BGG and Ludifolie Editions for more information!

title: More Aggressive Attitudes, 1862 Virginia Campaign
description: Designed by John Thiessen.  Artwork by Amabel Holland and Patrick Tremoureux.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Quick playing GCACW lite game covering the 2nd Manassas Campaign at the Corps level. See BGG , Hollandspiele Games and Wargame Vault for more information!

title: Moscow Attacked!
description:
Designed by Louis R. Coatney.  Artwork by Louis R. Coatney.
By kind permission of Mr. Coatney.
notes: Conversion by Unknown; if you know, please leave a message on ZT Forums. Moscow Attacked is one of Lou Coatney's various FREE Games available on his site.  It deals with the German's attempts to conquer the Soviet Capital, before the onset of Winter during 1941. See BGG and Coatney History for more information! An older ZT1 ZTB, as found in the Geralt Collection.  Submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Mouse Guard:  Swords & Strongholds
description: Designed by Luke Crane. Artist, David Petersen, collaborated with designer, Luke Crane, to create this abstract strategy game that Mr. Petersen had depicted in his comic/graphic novel, "Mouse Guard."
notes: Conversion by Eric Sprague. A light strategy game for two players, from the setting of the Mouse Guard comics and roleplaying game. Did not use art from actual game. Board drawn by Eric Sprague. Card art created with icons from game-icons.net. Mouse pawns created from art by Carla Gom. See BGG , MouseGuard & Burning Wheel for more information!

title: Mr. Jack in New York - Po Polsku
description:
Designed by Bruno Cathala, Ludovic Maublanc.  Artistry by Pierô.
Awards: 2010 Golden Geek Best 2-Player Board Game Nominee!
ZT Note: Because of the nature of components, multi-language play possible!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  Suspected of being the terrible Ripper, Francis J. Tumblety, the self-proclaimed doctor, is arrested by the London police service. He then escapes to New-York, where witnesses see him. The local police will not be deceived, as rumors suggest that he is in Manhattan, where the crimes appear strangely like they did in London. The police take no chance and ask the most eminent people of the city to help them in the chase of The Ripper. You will need to Investigate whether Francis J. Tumblety the real Mr. Jack, or if it is someone else. Mr. Jack in New-York is a complete game all on its own, however it is recommend for a beginner to play Mr. Jack first. The new version is more complex and requires more strategy. Mr. Jack is exclusively published by Hurrican, all printings of Mr. Jack are from Hurrican Games and distributed by other companies See BGG , HUrrican Games and Rebel.PL for more information!

title: Mr. Jack w Londynie - Po Polsku
description: Designed by Bruno Cathala and Ludovic Maublanc. Artistry by Pierô. Awards: Multiple Awards Winner, see BGG entry for full list!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  The search is on!  Can Jack the Ripper be found before another victim falls?  A classic Murder/Mystery game. See BGG and Hurrican Games for more information!

title: Mr. Lincoln's War:  Army of the Potomac AND Tennessee
description: Combined games of Army of the Potomac AND Tennessee.  As designed by Mark McLaughlin and originally arted by Rodger B. MacGowan.  This ZTB has Updated Map & Counter art by J Todd.
notes: Conversion by Jerry Todd.  Mr. Lincoln's War is a historical game which captures the epic struggle of the American Civil War. Mr. Lincoln's War is organized into two games, the Army of the Tennessee, which deals with the western theater, and The Army of the Potomac, which deals with the war in Virginia. See: BGG1 & BGG2 and Uhlan Games for further information!

title: Mukden, 1905: Russia vs. Japan
description: Designed by Richard Spence.  During this period in our hobby, artists were not always attributed.  If you know the original artist, please leave a message on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. The largest land battle fought, before WWI (610K troops with 164K casualties).  A streamlind  simulation of this decisive battle versus other wargames of the period. See BGG for and Wikipedia more information!

title: Musket Diplomacy
description: Designed by Jerry Todd.  As arted by Jerry Todd.  As Updated 12/13/2021.
notes: Conversion by Jerry Todd.  A Napoleonic Wars flavored multi-player campaign game for up to 6 players based on Avalon Hill's War and Peace, Blitzkrieg, and Diplomacy.  See BGG and Uhlan Games for MORE - rules available!

title: Mustangs
description:
Designer Samuel Craig Taylor, Jr.  Artist, Charles J. Kibler II.
Historical Note:  ZT2's FIRST SUBMISSION (2/14/2022)!
notes: Converted for ZunTzu in 2009 by Pokke.  Plane-to-Plane Combat in WW2.  Thanks to Pokke for re-submitting the 'lost' ZTB from ZT1st site! For further information, see BGG and Avalon Hill . . .

title: Mutant Chronicles - Siege on the Citadel 1st Ed
description: Designer Mr. Richard Berg. Graphics by Paul Bonner.
notes: Conversion by Primeevil.  Precursor of the Mutant Chronicles miniatures Game and a kissing cousin of Heroquest stands Mutant Chronicles: The Siege of the Citadel. See BGG , Casper Games and Pressman Toys for further information!

title: Napoleon and the Archduke Charles
description: Published in two parts in Strategy & Tactics #113 and #114. Designed by Keith Poulter. Map by EarthSurface Graphics. Counters by Larry Hoffman.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for all the two-map scenarios published in S&T #115, S&T #116, and Wargamer v.2 #3; defaults to the five-day scenario. See BGG here and here for more information. For more information, see Decision Games (DG)

title: Napoleon at Borodino
description: Designed by Randy Pippus (self -published) for use at the Fandom II gaming convention.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  A game on the battle of Borodino patterned after SPI's mini, Napoleon at Waterloo. It has a number of movement allowances per turn for the French and their Allies (12 units) and the Russian (10 units), making it a matter of constantly allocating limited resources to achieve objectives. As an added fillip, units in ZoCs count against the movement allowance. See BGG for more information!

title: Napoleon at War
description: Designed by Edward Curran, Thomas Walczyk, David C. Isby, Irad B. Hardy, and Frank Davis. Physical systems design and graphics by Redmond A. Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  An SPI Quad game containing four separate Napoleonic battles: Marengo (subtitle: Napoleon in Italy, 14 June 1800) Jena-Auerstadt (subtitle: The Battle for Prussia 14 October 1806) Wagram (subtitle: The Peace of Vienna, 5-6 July 1809) The Battle of Nations (subtitle: The Encirclement at Leipzig, 16-19 October 1813). Setups provided for all games in a single scenario file. See BGG & DG (Decision Games) for more information.

title: Napoleon at Waterloo
description: Designed by James Dunnigan. Original graphics by Redmond.  Introductory level treatment of the battle of Waterloo. With Rules.  This download is in ZIP format.  Please unzip to see the ZTB and other items.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan This was a free game given out in the early days of SPI to increase the "hobby base." As such it was designed to be a simple introductory game for beginners but still be interesting and challenging enough for experienced wargamers. They succeeded. NAW is a fun, exciting and tense "beer and pretzels" game. This gamebox includes the Historical and Grouchy Variant scenarios. It also includes the 4-page Rulebook right within the gamebox as a separate "scenario." (The "scenario" opens in "terrain mode" which is the easiest way to read the rules in ZunTzu.) The counters and map are done in the 1979 graphics. See BGG and DG for further information!

title: Napoleon at Waterloo PLUS (New Graphics with rules)
description: Designed by James Dunnigan. Original graphics by Redmond Simonsen.  Grouchy Variant by A.A. Nofi.  New graphics by Mr. Matthijs van der Zanden!  This download is in ZIP format. Please unzip to see the ZTB and other items.
notes: Conversion by Anonymous.  Original artwork by Matthijs van der Zanden. This download is in ZIP format. Please unzip to see the ZTB and extras! See BGG , DG and kobudovenlo or Kobudovenlo.nl New for more information (including Squad Leader aides)!

title: Napoleon on the Danube
description: Designed by Mark Hinkle.  Artists:  Jean Baptiste Édouard Detaille and Mark Hinkle.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  NES 1st game of Napoleonic Warfare on grand tactical scale. A simulation of the 1809 battle of (Deutsch-) Wagram, which was fought on July 5th-6th, 1809. The game is a Napoleon's Last Battles(NLB) scale and rule descendant: - scale = 480 m/ hex - time = 60 min/ Game Turn - strength = 450-650 men/ Strength Point See BGG and NES-Games for further information!

title: Napoleon Retreats
description:
Designed by Kevin Zucker. Counters and maps by Charlie Kibler. Charts and tables by Brendan Clark. Part of the Library of Napoleonic Battles.
Awards:  2019 Charles S. Roberts Best Napoleonic Era Board Wargame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Cards not included. Although this ZTB can be used to play any of the individual battles, it is specifically designed to support the combined campaign game. Winter 1814: Hope Against Hope.  An exciting game using a tried and true system! See BGG for & Napoleon Games (OSG?) for more information.

title: Napoleon's Art of War: Dresden
description: Designer Omar DeWittBob Dervis, Ollie Johansson, Bob Pollard and Redmond Askel Simonsen.  Graphics by Jean Baptiste Édouard Detaille and Redmond Askel Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Battle of Dresden. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Napoleon's Battles et. al. PLUS+
description: Designed by Robert L. Coggins and Craig Taylor, Jr.  Artist(s) are Unknown.  Should you know, please leave a message on ZT forums!  This ZTB includes the Core game and both Modules (1&2).
notes: Conversion by Massimo Finocchiaro (aka Maaaax, & MaxFin). This game is a traditional 15mm Napoleonic Miniatures rules set. The basic game covers weather, routing, command & control, movement & maneuver, defensive reaction, fire, combat, and pursuit.  Advanced and optional rules add depth in the areas of fatigue, morale, evasion, special cavalry rules, supply chains, hidden movement, and generals.  Also, as a PLUS+ design, please use the ZT user interface (UIC) to access scenarios etc. NOTE#1:  see included TAB named "Read Me First." NOTE#2:  This ZT design is a must see for how to handle minature games within ZunZtu! See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information!

title: Napoleon's Danube Campaign
description:
Copyright 1984, Victory Games, a subsidary of Avalon Hill Games
Designer Kevin Zucker
Artists: Ted Koller, James Talbot
Awards & Honors
    1984 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-Twentieth Century Game Nominee
notes: Conversion by Mitch King This game uses Kevin Zucker's operational Napoleonic campaign system to cover Napoleon's defeat of Austria in his 1809 campaign.  The game systems assigns limited administrative resources to each side, combined with command control issues to make for a challenging system.  The game box includes setups for the four scenarios.  See BGG for more information and Kevin Zucker's Designer's Notes .  One player must own a copy of Victory Game's "1809: Napoleon's Danube Campaign" in order to use this game box.

title: Napoleon's First Battles (DG)
description: Designed by Joseph Miranda.  As arted by Douglas S. Chaffee and Joy Cohn.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Napoleon's First Battles simulates four early battles from the French Republican era, namely, "Montenotte", "Arcola", "The Pyramids" and "Marengo". See BGG and DG (Decsion Games) for more information!

title: Napoleon's Last Battles
description: Designed by Kevin Zucker.  Graphics: Larry Elmore, Trevor Holman and Redmond Askel Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Napoleon's Last Battles depicts the last campaign of Napoleon: the Waterloo Campaign (1815). It contains 4 individual battles (with own counters and maps): Quatre Bras, Ligny, Wavre, La Belle Alliance (Waterloo) and a campaign game linking all 4 maps and covering the whole campaign. See BGG and DG for further information!

title: Napoleon's Triumph
description: Designed by Bowen Simmons.  As arted by Jean-Louis Ernest Meissonier.  Awards: 2008 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee; 2008 Golden Geek Best 2-Player Board Game Nominee; 2007 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Napoleon’s Triumph is built on the same foundations as its acclaimed predecessor, Bonaparte at Marengo, but is bigger and grander in scale. It uses two boards to make a double-size 44" x 34" map of the Austerlitz battlefield and has twice as many pieces as the earlier game, but defying the tradition that big wargames must also take a long time to play, Napoleon’s Triumph can be played from start to finish in a single evening. See BGG for further information!

title: Napoleon's Triumph
description: Designed by Bowen Simmons.  As arted by Jean-Louis Ernest Meissonier.  Awards: 2008 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee; 2008 Golden Geek Best 2-Player Board Game Nominee; 2007 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. On December 2, 1805, on the battlefield of Austerlitz, an outnumbered French army led by their newly crowned emperor, Napoleon, waited to receive an expected attack by a Russian and Austrian army commanded by the Russian Czar, Alexander. Napoleon lured the Allies into attacking with their left wing, and when the Allies did so, a surprise French counter-attack smashed the Allied right and centre, and then surrounded and destroyed the Allied left in one of the most famous and decisive battles in military history. See BGG for further information!

title: Napoleon's Wheel
description: Designed by Kevin Zucker. Graphics by Knut Grunitz, Charlie Kibler, Christopher Moeller, and Brandan Clark. Part of The Library of Napoleonic Battles.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for most scenarios. Cards not included. See BGG for more info.

title: Napoleonic Empire
description: Designed by Lloyd Krassner.  Artist's unknown; please place a post on ZT Forums - if known.  An original ZT1 - found by Mr. E. Sprague . . .
notes: Conversion by Joao. Give me Empire or give me Elba! Cards, Counters, and Map included! "Two player strategic war game set in the Napoleonic era. One player controls France & Napoleon. The other player controls the Allies. The allies include England, Russia, Prussia, and Austria." See BGG & WarpSpawnGames for more information! Please note that this was an older ZT1 game found in E. Sprague's Hard-Drive!  Do you have another ZT1 ZTB?

title: Napoleons Last Battles (SPI)
description: Designed by Kevin Zucker.  Graphics: Larry Elmore, Trevor Holman and Redmond Askel Simonsen (all editions).
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Napoleon's Last Battles depicts the last campaign of Napoleon: the Waterloo Campaign (1815). It contains 4 individual battles (with own counters and maps): Quatre Bras Ligny Wavre La Belle Alliance (Waterloo) and a campaign game linking all 4 maps and covering the whole camapign. The latest DG edition adds three more scenarios, including a Grand Waterloo battle scenario. See BGG and DG for more information.

title: NATO: The Next War in Europe
description:
NATO: The Next War in Europe is an operational level simulation of potential NATO/Warsaw Pact conflict in Central Europe
Bruce S. Maxwell, Richard J. Trup.  Graphics by Ted Koller (four Charles S. Roberts Awards for Best Wargame Graphics between 1984 and 1988 while working for Victory Games: Vietnam 1965 - 1975, Pax Britannica, Korean War, and Lee vs. Grant (tied for the award with Rick Barber for The Campaigns of Robert E. Lee).
notes: Conversion by bggames01. "NATO: The Next War in Europe" is a highly acclaimed operational level simulation of potential NATO/Warsaw Pact conflict in Central Europe.  This ZTB uses original counters. Includes Strategic Surprise, Tactical Surprise, Extended Build-Up scenarios pre-setup.  Includes extra counters required to play The War of Nerves (new scenario) and The War of Nerves (1981 Variant). See BGG , BGGames01 and modern Avalon Hill for more information!

title: Newtonia: The Civil War on the Missouri Border
description: Designed by Lawrence P. Duffield. Digitally published by LPD Games as part of its Battles of the American Civil War series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for both scenarios. Newtonia is a game designed to test new rules concepts for the Battles of the American Civil War series. There were two battles outside this tiny Missouri town, one in 1862 as the Confederacy sought to tap the agricultural produce and mineral resources of the surrounding region, and another in late 1864 when Sterling Price’s Army of Missouri sought a brief rest during its retreat after the Battle of Westport. Each scenario exemplifies a different tactical situation. See BGG for more information!

title: Next  War, The  v2  (SPI)
description: Designed by James F. Dunnigan. Graphic design by Redmond A. Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon, based on images available at SPI Wargaming Resources . Campaign scenario setup by Dan Davis. See BGG for more information.

title: Next War, The: Modern Conflict in Europe
description:
Designed by James F. Dunnigan& Mark Herman.  An early work by Redmond Askel Simonsen.
Awards:  1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Twentieth Century Game Nominee.  1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Graphics and Physical Systems Nominee!
notes: Conversion by Luiz Cláudio. The Next War is a brigade/divisional level simulation of a Soviet-led Warsaw Pact invasion of the central European front of NATO in the late 1970's. The three maps cover the area from the far north of Denmark, through Germany and Austria to the industrial heartland of Italy. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: No Retreat! (Including Solitaire Kit) v1.0
description:
The War in Russia During WW2.
Designed by Carl Paradis.  Artwork by Rodger B. MacGowan and Mark Simonitch.  Also included is the VPG/C3i Solitaire Kit.
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett No Retreat! is a two-player grand strategic level wargame depicting the struggle between the Axis powers and the Soviet Union during World War 2 from the start of Operation Barbarossa on June 22, 1941 (the invasion of Russia) to the final surrender of Germany in 1945. At Least one player must own a physical copy of game - to download and play! See BGG , GMT (& VPG) for further information!

title: Nordkapp
description:
Designed by Charles Tustin Kamps and Edward G. Sollers.  As arted by Ivor M. Janci, Keith Parkinson and Stephen D. Sullivan.
As first seen in Strategy and Tactics Magazine #94.
We are unsure if this ZTB was ever included on ZT1, hence the categorization of "NEW/Reupload?" . . .
notes: Convertor Unknown (Steelwhip?),  Nordkapp is a two player game covering potential warfare between NATO and the USSR in the area of Scandinavia north of the Arctic Circle. Found in Steelwhip ZTB archive (2024, still active).  Should you have any corrections or additions, please leave a post on ZT Forums. See BGG and DG (Decision Games) for more game information!

title: Normandy'44
description:
Designed by Mark Simonitch.  As arted by Rodger B. MacGowan and Mark Simonitch.
Awards:  2010 Charles S. Roberts Best World War 2 Era Board Wargame Winner. 2010 Charles S. Roberts Best World War 2 Era Board Wargame Nominee.
2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Board Game Graphics Winner. 2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Board Game Graphics Nominee.
notes: Conversion by Luiz Cláudio. Normandy '44 is a 2, 3, or 4-player, regimental level game of the D-Day landings on June 6th and the battles that raged in Normandy for the next 21 days. At Least one player must own a physical copy of game - to download and play! See BGG and GMT for more information!

title: North Africa '41
description:
Designer: Mark Simonitch
Artists: Antonis Karidis, Mark Simonitch
 Awards & Honors
    2023 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  This game box expands GMT Game's North Africa '41 to include the Italian offensive into Egypt in September, 1940 and Operation Compass, the British counter-offensive to drive the Italians back out.  The game scale is battalion/regiment/brigade sized units with 8 miles/hex and half month turns with two to three impulses per turn.  See BGG and GMT Games for more information about this expansion game.   One of the players in the game MUST own a physical copy of GMT Game's "North Africa '41" to use this game box.

title: Not War But Murder (Ato #19) 1.0
description:
Designed by Michael Rinella. As arted by Craig Granado.
Users should own original game.
The Cold Harbour Campaign, Union campaign to capture Richmond, May 27-June 3, 1864.
notes: Conversion by federico67 (from ZT1). Users should own original game. The Cold Harbour Campaign, Union campaign to capture Richmond, May 27-June 3, 1864. See BGG and ATO for more information! A well respected Civil War game!

title: Notre Dame
description:
Designed by Stefan Feld.  As arted by Harald Lieske,
Awards: 2008 JoTa Best Light Board Game Nominee; 2008 Golden Geek Best Gamer's Board Game Nominee; 2008 Boardgames Australia Awards Best International Game Nominee; 2007 Tric Trac Nominee; 2007 Spiel des Jahres Recommended; 2007 Meeples Choice Award Nominee; 2007 International Gamers Awards - General Strategy; Multi-player Nominee; 2007 Golden Geek Best Gamer's Board Game Nominee; 2007 Golden Geek Best Family Board Game Nominee; 2007 Golden Geek Best Board Game Artwork/Presentation Nominee; 2007 Deutscher Spiele Preis Best Family/Adult Game 2nd Place
notes: Converter is unknown, please leave a message on ZT Forums, should you have information.  In the shadow of the Notre Dame cathedral, players compete for prosperity and reputation. This is an older ZT1 ZTB as found in the "Zwever Collection." See BGG and Rio Grande Games for more information!

title: O'Connor's Offensive V1.2
description:
Designed by Vance von Borries. Originally published in Wargamer #41.
This was one of a series of seven games that all use a common system. The System was called "Battles for North Africa". The other games in the group were Decision at Kasserine: Rommel's Last Chance (the original), Hellfire Pass, Rommel at Bay, Patton Goes to War, Objective: Tunis, and Race for Tunis.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setup provided for Scenario 1. An operational scale game of combat between the Allies and Italians in the North African Desert in World War II. This update features the following enhancements: * Free-floating charts. * Starting units for Scenario 1 placed on the map. * Added the small marker sheet from Decision at Kasserine. Find other such ZTBs in our ZT library. For more info, see BGG .

title: Objective: Kiev v1.0
description: Designed by Frank Chadwick.  Arted by Alan Emrich, Rodger B. MacGowan and Mark Simonitch.
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett. "Objective: Kiev is a new historical board game from renowned game designer Frank Chadwick, iterating the classic Battle for Moscow game system used in The Arduous Beginning, combining ease of learning and design elegance with the kind of dramatic gameplay that Frank has long been famous for. Featuring countless opportunities and variations, Objective: Kiev presents an endlessly fascinating series of puzzles and is a game that you're going to want to play again and again." See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Objective: Tunis
description:
Designed by Vance von Borries. Published in Strategy & Tactics #140. Part of the Battles for North Africa series.
ZT Designers: see this version, an excellent example of how ZT design is "open ended."
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Includes setups (on the organization charts) for both scenarios. The ZTB incorporates all of the copious errata to the map, charts, and counters, as published in subsequent issues of S&T. For more info, see BGG and Decision Games !

title: Ocania 1809
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey.  Original artist, Pascal da Silva.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. Ocaña (November 19 1809, Spain) are the 27e and 28e battles of the series Jours de Gloire. See BGG and Canons en Carton for more information!

title: October War
description:
Designed by Irad "Terry" B. Hardy, III.  As arted by Redmond Askel Simonsen.
AWARDS: 1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Nominee.
notes: Conversion by J. Patterson. This game is a tactical simulation of combat in the Middle East during the 1973 Yom Kippur War. The game included a map, 200 counters representing Israeli and Arab forces, and a 12-page rulebook. See BGG & DG for more information!

title: Okehazama 1560 (日本の進撃) - English & Japanese
description: Designed by Yamazaki Masahiro. Originally published in the Spring 1995 issue of Six Angles magazine, but subsequently reissued by Sunset Games in 2002 as part of the Six Angles Collection.
notes: Conversions by T. Gordon. Players play the battle of Japanese Daimyo.  Setup provided. Charts in English and Japanese. See BGG , Six Angles and Sunset Games for more information.

title: Okko: Era of the Asagrii - En Français
description:
Designed by Laurent Pouchain.  Artistry by Hub, also known as Humbert Chabuel, François Lecocq and Geoffrey Stepourneko.
We are unsure of Publisher, please inform us on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by Laurent BARESSE, The Gamebox contains materials of : Okko: Era of the Asagiri Okko: Era of the Karasu Okko: Yakuza Hazu Akai Okko: Pajan Gun'Taï and some additional features found on the official web site. See BGG for further information! An older ZT1 ZTB found in Geralt Collection by R. Peterson.

title: Olympica
description:
Designed by Lynn Willis.  As originally arted by Jennell Jaquays.
Revised map and counters by David Little (used with permission).
Metagaming Microgame No. 7.
notes: Conversion by Eric Sprague. OLYMPICA simulates the U.N. Mars raid to capture the Web Mind Generator from a heavily defended area near Nix Olympica's massive caldera. See BGG for more information!

title: On To Paris 1870 - 1871:  The Franco-Prussian War
description: Designed by Milan Becvar and as arted by Timothy Schleif.
notes: Conversion by  David Jones.  On To Paris! uses a wargame system adapted from Victory Games' “The Civil War” to simulate the grand events of the Franco Prussian war (1870-71) and challenge players to control the leadership, organization and military operations of Armies and Corps during the later 19th century. See BGG and Compass Games for further information!

title: On to Richmond II-1862 (MMP Edition)
description:
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski, Ed Beach
Map Artwork: Charles Kibler
Counter Artists: Nicolás Eskubi, Charles Kibler
Awards & Honors
    2023 Charles S. Roberts Best New Edition of a Previously Published Game Winner
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  On to Richmond II is part of the Great Battles of the Civil War series.  This covers the action in Virginia from April to June, 1862.  The game box includes setups for all twelve scenarios.  See BGG and Multi-Man Publishing for more details.  One player must own "On to Richmond II" to use this game box.

title: On to Richmond II-Grant Takes Command
description:
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski, Ed Beach
Map Artwork: Charles Kibler
Counter Artists: Nicolás Eskubi, Charles Kibler
Awards & Honors

    2023 Charles S. Roberts Best New Edition of a Previously Published Game Winner

See BGG and Multi-Man Publishing for more details.  One player must own On to Richmond II to use this game box.
