title: On To Richmond! (AH Edition)
description: Designed by Joseph M. Balkoski and Ed Beach.  As originally arted by Charles J. Kibler II and Keith Rocco.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  This is the sixth game in the Great Campaigns of the American Civil War series. It covers the Peninsula campaign. See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information.

title: Onslaught: D-Day to the Rhine
description:
Designed by Douglas Niles.  As arted by Sawshun Tamaguchi.
Re-published in Command Magazine Japan, #64.
notes: Conversion by bggames01.  Wargame based around the WW2 Western Allied campaign from just after the Normandy invasion to the crossing of the Rhine. See BGG and DG for further information!

title: Operacao Littorio
description: Designed by D.H. Casciano. Graphics by M. Fisher.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. From the introduction: "Littorio explores military actions which could occur in South America should Brazil decide to use its vast resources and population to exert its dominance on the rest of the continent by military means." See BGG for more information.

title: Opération Apocalypse
description: Designed by Philippe Richardot.  Graphics by Didier Bourgeois.  Insert Vae Victis n°10
notes: Conversion by Convertie par Provence. Avec l'aimable autorisation d'Histoire et Collections.  Jeu en solitaire simulant un affrontement durant la guerre du Viet Nam. See BGG and Vae Victis for further information!

title: Operation Battleaxe, Wavell vs. Rommel, 1941
description: Designed by Michael Rinella.  Arted by Charles J. Kibler II.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Operation Battleaxe: Wavell vs. Rommel, 1941 is a quick-playing depiction of the June 1941 Allied offensive in the North African desert.  Utilizing a new and streamlined version of the “area-impulse” system players will experience the uncertainty of the desert battlefield. Each turn will contain a variable number of impulses, and both players will be challenged to determine whether it is better to attack first, or defend and then counter-attack. See BGG and Revolution Games for more information!

title: Operation Michael
description: Designed by John Best and Dean Essig.  Artist Unknown - if known, please inform on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by D. Deitch.  Sub-titled: 'Ludendorff's Last Chance' & Part of the Standard Combat Series #9, this game covers the March 21, 1918, offensive by the Germans in order to regain the initiative on the Western Front before the might of the U.S. forces will be felt. See BGG and MMP for further information!

title: Operation Rainbow (ニイタカヤマノボレ) - in English & 日本語
description:
Designed by Daisuke Sato. Second game set in the Hokkaido Republic alternative history timeline.
ZT Note:  An interesting ZT design option, in how this allows BOTH Japanese and English!  A must see for every ZT game designer!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English and Japanese (note that the English-language charts on the map are terrain pieces that can be removed to reveal the original Japanese versions). I have added Romanized names to the counters for Japanese leaders and naval units. Setup provided for the Grand Campaign, which is identical to that for the Short Campaign other than the reinforcements. See BGG for more information.

title: Operation Typhoon: The German Assault on Moscow
description: Designed by Joseph Angiolillo and Joseph M. Balkoski. Graphics by Redmond A. Simonsen.  It uses a variation of the Panzergruppe Guderian system.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setup provided for a Campaign Game. This is a big game, three maps but is a very playable monster game and a terrific multi player game. It was the first SPI game to use the concept of variable unit strength. Units are rated for size and morale but actual strengths (fog of war) are determined by drawing a chit randomly at the point where your unit first enters combat. See BGG and DG and Hobby Japan for more information!

title: Operation Veritable v1.0
description: Designed by Paul Rohrbaugh. Development by Alan Emrich.  Many thanks to Alan Emrich for allowing this to exist!
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett. The Battle for the Reichswald: Feb. - Mar. 1945.    Ownership of original boardgame required... See BGG and VPG for further information!

title: Operation Weserübung
description: Design and artwork by Éric Grenier.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon Operation Weserübung: The Invasion of Norway covers the German invasion of Norway in 1940 during World War II. The game covers all aspects of the invasion, including land, naval, and air operations as well as the British and French involvement. See BGG for more information.

title: Ordered to Die
description: Designed by Dennis Bishop. Map by Tim Allen. Counter art by Lionel Liron.  A rare game of this battle.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Ordered to Die is a Dennis L. Bishop simulation of the WW1 November, 1915, battle of Ctesiphon in Iraq. See BGG & White Dog Games for more information.

title: Oregon
description:
Designed by Ase Berg, Henrik Berg.  Art by Franz Vohwinkel.

Awards:  2009 Boardgames Australia Awards Best International Game Nominee; 2008 Vuoden Peli Family Game of the Year Nominee; 2008 Golden Geek Best Family Board Game Nominee; 2008 Årets Spill Best Family Game Nominee.
notes: Conversion by loic_425.  Oregon is a family/strategy game with a colonization-theme and a card-driven placement mechanism. The aim of the game is to position farmers and point-giving buildings in the best possible locations on the board. See BGG , Rio Grande Games and Hans Im Gluck for more information! An older ZT1 ZTB found in the Geralt Collection by R. Peterson.

title: Orris's Storm: The Battle of Stamford Bridge
description: Designed by Norman Smith.  Artist Unknown - please inform on ZT Forums.
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  This sister game to Senlac Hill covers King Harold's great victory over the Vikings in York at Stamford Bridge, before his great defeat by the Normans in southern England a little over a week later. Includes rules for Berserk Vikings and uses "untried units" in the Viking setup so that neither player knows their combat value until they fight. See BGG and Saxon Games for further information!

title: Over There
description: Designed by A. E. Goodwin and Eric Pierce.  Artists unattributed.  Should you know, please post on ZT Forums.
notes: Conversion by Luiz Cláudio. A game of the 1918 campaigns on the Western and Italian Fronts during World War One, using units that are mostly divisions and brigades, with two-week turns, and maps at 16 miles per hex. Optional scenarios extend the war into 1919-1920, and allow Over There to be mated with the game March to Victory: West Front 1914-1916 to play out all of World War One in the West from 1914 to 1920. See BGG and GRD for more information!

title: Overlord, 1st Edition
description: Designed by John Hill.  The Conflict version has not verified artist attribution.  Should you know, please leave a post on ZT Forums!  Note: There is a 2nd Edition produced by GDW.
notes: Conversion by T Gordon. "Overlord" is an operational wargame of the Allied invasion and breakout from the Normandy peninsula.  Including the periods of the Cobra Breakout, the German Mortain Counteroffensive, and the cataclysmic Battle of the Falaise Pocket, which broke the back of German armor in the West. See BGG for more information.

title: Pan Lodowego Ogrodu (The Lord of The Ice Garden) 1.0 - Po Polsku
description:
Designed by Krzysztof Wolicki.  Graphics by Dominik Kasprzycki.
ZT Note: Nice 3-D minis!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  The world of Midgaard, created by author Jarosław Grzędowicz in The Lord of the Ice Garden novel series, is inhabited by a race very similar to humans, filled with magic and for a reason stuck at the cultural and technological level of medieval Viking world. The arrival of scientists from Earth disturbs its fragile balance. The power gained by controlling magic changes the scientists – they become possessed by the lust for making this world better. They become gods, who are willing to sacrifice any life, except for their own, of course, to accomplish their – great, according to them – ideas. See BGG and Redimp Games for more information!

title: Pancho Villa Dead or Alive!
description: Designed by Phil Eklund.  Artist's unknown.  Should you know the artists', please inform on ZT Forums!  "History requires this" . . . for such an excellent game!
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  The 1916 expedition of General Pershing and the US Army to punish the Mexican outlaw bandit, Pancho Villa. Chase the wily bandit leader throughout the Sierra Madre, while trying not to get lost, destroy your horses, or get into trouble with the local carrancistas. See BGG and Ion Games for more information!

title: Pandemic - en Español
description:
Designed by Matt Leacock.  Artwork by Josh Cappel; Christian Hanisch; Regis Moulun; and Thomas Theil.
Awards: 40+ - see BGG entry for full list!
notes: Conversión por desconocido. Si usted sabe, por favor deje un mensaje en los foros de ZT. Prevenir un brote pandémico mundial, mediante el tratamiento de los puntos calientes y la investigación de curas. Incluye escenarios de expansión 'On the Brink'. Se trata de una antigua ZT1 ZTB que se encuentra en las colecciones Geralt y Zwever. Presentado por R. Peterson. ¡Vea BGG y Z-Man Games para obtener más información!

title: Pandemic - in English
description:
Designed by Matt Leacock.  Artwork by Josh Cappel; Christian Hanisch; Regis Moulun; and Thomas Theil.
Awards: 40+ - see BGG entry for full list!
notes: Conversion by Unknown. If you know , please leave a post on ZT Forums. Prevent a worldwide pandemic outbreak, by treating hot spots and researching cures. Includes 'On the Brink' expansion scenarios. This an old ZT1 ZTB found in the Geralt and Zwever Collections. As Submitted by R. Peterson. See BGG and Z-Man Games for more information!

title: Panzer Leader, Tactical Warfare on the Western Front
description: Designer Dave Clark, Randall C. Reed and Nick Smith.  As originally arted by W. Scott Moores and Randall C. Reed.
notes: Conversion by Alejo (?) - see ZT Forum . Continuing from the Panzerblitz heritage, Panzer Leader is focused on WW2 western front.  An exceptional game in understanding post invasion tactics. See BGG and modern Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Panzerarmee Afrika, Rommel in the Desert, April '41 to Dec. '42
description: Designed by James F. Dunnigan.  As arted by Rodger B. MacGowan and Redmond Askel Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  PanzerArmee Afrika: Rommel in the Desert, April 1941 - November 1942", is a wargame simulation of the North African Campaign between April 1941 and November 1942. Battalion, Regiment and Brigade-sized units represent the actual forces which took part in the fighting. Included in the game is a Variable Orders-of-Battle Chart that offers variations in forces to demonstrate how history might have been different. See BGG and Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Panzerblitz 1st Edition
description: Designed by the famous James F. Dunnigan.  As arted by Redmond Askel Simonsen.  As a hidden extra I have put the situation cards #14 - 25 on the reverse side of the situation #1 - 12 cards.
notes: Conversion by Andrew.  Avalon Hills groundbreaking tactical-scale board wargame of armored combat set in the Eastern Front of the Second World War.  A well done ZT version - - pay attention to 'Terrains' to get the maps! See BGG and modern Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Panzergruppe Guderian PLUS+
description: Designed by James F. Dunnigan as arted by Rodger B. MacGowan and Redmond Aksel Simonsen.  As first seen in S&T #57.
notes: Converson by Maaaax .  Wargame simulation of the German campaign to capture Smolensk in July, 1941. See BGG and Decision Games for more information!

title: Paths of Glory
description:
Designed by Ted Raicer.  Graphics (all versions) by Charles J. Kibler II, Terry Leeds, Rodger B. MacGowan and Mark Simonitch.
Awards:  2000 International Gamers Awards - Historical Simulation.  1999 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargame Graphics Nominee.  1999 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Boardgame Winner.  1999 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Boardgame Nominee!!!!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  Should you know this author, let us know on ZT forums!  Card driven strategic simulation of World War I. At least one player must own a physical copy of game - to download and play! See BGG and GMT for further information!

title: Patton Goes to War V1.2
description:
Designed by Vance von Borries. Map graphics by Rodger B. MacGowan and Randal Thomson. Published in Strategy & Tactics #112. Part of the Battles for North Africa series.
Awards: 1987 Charles S. Roberts Best World War II Board Game Nominee!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Patton Goes to War is a two-player operational level simulation of the World War II American offensive in southern Tunisia led by Gen. George S. Patton, which took place between March 16th and April 3rd 1943. It was first published in Strategy & Tactics magazine #112. This update features the following enhancements: * Counter resolution upgraded to 400 dpi. * Free-floating charts. * Starting units for Scenario 4 placed on the map (all other pieces remain on the organization charts). * Added the small marker sheet from Decision at Kasserine. For more info see BGG & DG .

title: Patton's Best 1.0
description: Designed by Bruce Shelley.  Graphics by Charles J. Kibler II and George Ira Parrish, Jr.
notes: Conversion by Gary Krockover.  Solitaire game of tank command.  This is a solitaire game involving tank command-- that is you control a Sherman tank (17 variations) and command a crew assigned to the 4th Armored Division as you move out of the "Cobra Breakout" following the Normandy invasion. See BGG and modern Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Paul Koenig's - D-Day, The American Beaches
description: Designed by Paul Koenig.  As arted by Alan Emrich.
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett.  Problems galore in this invasion's battle.  Can you overcome the problems?  Play and see . . . See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Paul Koenig's - D-Day: The Canadian Beaches
description: Designed by Paul Koenig Artwork by Alan Elmrich.
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett.  Paul Koenig's - D-Day, Canadian Beaches. See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Paul Koenig's D-Day: American & Canadian Beaches
description: Victory Points Games about the D-Day invasion.  Designed by Paul Koenig.  Arted by Alan Emrich.
notes: Conversion by BGGames01.  A combined game of Paul Koenig's D-Day.  This ZTB includes both American & Canadian Beachheads. See BGGames01 and VPG for further information!

title: Pea Ridge
description:
Designer: Chris Perello.  Artist: Joseph Youst.
This is the DG version.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge. Pea Ridge uses the Musket & Saber system to accurately portray warfare during the American Civil War. See BGG and DG for more information

title: Pea Ridge: The Gettysburg of the West
description:
Orginal Game System Designer: Richard Berg
Designer: Eric Lee Smith
Map Graphics: Redmond Simonsen
Zun Tzu Counters: Mitch King
Awards & Honors:
1980 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee
notes: Conversion by Mitch King. Pea Ridge is a game in the Great Battles of the American Civil War series designed by Richard Berg, originator of this regimental game system with Terrible Swift Sword in 1976.  The game scale is 120 yards per hex, 100 man strength points and 20 minute game turns.  This game covers Earl Van Dorn's Confederates attacked Samuel Curtis' Army of the Southwest northeast of Fayetteville, AK on March 7-8, 1862.  The game box uses the counters created by Mitch King. See BGG and Armchair Brigade for more details.  One player must own SPI's "Pea Ridge" to use this game box.

links.url: https://zuntzu.com/gameboxes/SPI&SandT&TSR&DG/Pea Ridge_ The Gettysburg of the West.ztb

title: Pegasus Bridge, The Beginning of D-Day
description:
Designed by Robert G. Markham and Mark Seaman.  Artist: Rodger B. MacGowan.  Awards:  	
1988 Charles S. Roberts Best World War II Board Game Nominee & 1988 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargaming Graphics Nominee.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  A tactical level solitaire game of the British assault on the Orne River bridges on D-Day. Published as an issue game in Strategy & Tactics magazine #122, November - December 1988. Similar in style to Markham's solitaire treatment of the Raid on St. Nazaire. See BGG and MarkhamDesigns for further information!

title: Pente 5th ed
description:
Designed by Gary Gabrel & Tom Braunlich.  Artist Gary Gabrel. 
This is a Zip File.  Please download and open ZIP file for Rules and ZTB!
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan Pente is a classic strategy game played with colored stones on a grid playing surface. The rules are simple. The moves can be complex. The pace is good--it doesn't bog down like chess sometimes can. This gamebox has three scenarios: a two-player setup with green and yellow stones, a four colored scenario adding blue and red stones, and a third "scenario" with a 6-page abbreviated rule section. Please download and open ZIP file for Rules and ZTB! See BGG for further information!

title: Pharsalus
description: Designed by Loren K. Wiseman.  During this period of our hobby, artists were not always attributed.  Should you know, please notate on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Simulates the land battle between Caesar and Pompey during the Roman Civil War, 48 B.C. This is a tactical-level battle game.  A decisive Battle during the Ronman Civil War. See BGG and FarFutures for more information!

title: Pièges Galactiques ZIP
description:
Designed by François Marcela-Froideval.  Artist Unknown.
This is a ZIP file.
notes: Conversion by Provence.  Dans l'espace...vous pouvez toujours crier!  - - "In Space you can always scream!" Please download and unzip the file for Rules and ZTB!  Il s’agit d’un fichier ZIP.  Veuillez télécharger et décompresser le fichier pour Rules et ZTB! See BGG for more information!

title: Pilares de la Tierra, los - En Español
description:
Spanish edition of the Pillars of the Earth.
By Michael Rieneck and Stefan Stadler.  As arted by Michael Menzel, Anke Pohl and Thilo Rick Awards are many, please see BGG entry!
notes: Conversion by Zuntzuniacos.  Publisher maybe incorrect. Should you know please leave a message on ZT Forums! Contribute the most to the cathedral's construction. This an older ZT1 ZTB found in the Zwever Collection. See BGG and KOSMOS (?) for more information!

title: Pillars of the Earth, The - in English
description:
Designed by Michael Rieneck and Stefan Stadler.  As arted by Michael Menzel, Anke Pohl and Thilo Rick
Awards are many, please see BGG entry!
notes: Conveter & which publisher is unknown.  Should you know please leave a message on ZT Forums!  Contribute the most to the cathedral's construction. The cathedral is built by removing layers of terrain in the middle of the game board.  Enable terrain editing, then 'delete' one layer for each game round.  A new image of the cathedral will be revealed. This an older ZT1 ZTB as found in the Geralt Collection. See BGG and Kosmos for more information!

title: Pillars of the Earth, The (De Kathedraal) in Dutch?
description:
Dutch (?) edition of the Pillars of the Earth.
By Michael Rieneck and Stefan Stadler.  As arted by Michael Menzel, Anke Pohl and Thilo Rick Awards are many, please see BGG entry!
notes: Conveter & which exact publisher is unknown.  Should you know please leave a message on ZT Forums!  Contribute the most to the cathedral's construction. This seems to be a Dutch translation from Zuntzuniacos Spanish version. This is an older ZT1 ZTB as found in the Geralt & Zwever Collections. See BGG and Kosmos for more information!

title: Piotrków 1939
description: 3rd (boxed) edition. Designed by Wojciech Zalewski in collaboration with Krzysztof Wojdyło and Rafał Zalewski. Map by Piotr Promiński, Rafał Zalewski, and Wojciech Zalewski. Part of the Wrzesien 1939 series, but this edition uses the WB-95 system.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  The game simulates one of the biggest battles of the Polish Defensive War of 1939 that took place near the town of Piotrków Trybunalski from 5 to 6 September, 1939. After two-day fierce fighting, the Polish forces suffered a defeat and were forced to retreat. Charts in Polish and English. Setup provided for September 1st. See BGG & Taktyka i Strategia for more information.

title: PKMG: Arnhem Bridge v1.0
description: Design by Paul Koenig.  Graphics by Tim Allen and Bryan Armor.
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett. "Based upon the design of Paul Koenig's D-Day Series, Arnhem Bridge is the first to be released in the Market Garden series, covering all the events that happened there from September 17th-19th, 1944. Including a set of Optional Rules, make a stand against your enemies at Arnhem Bridge!" Two styles of counter graphics are supported in this gamebox - square (by default) and rounded. And you can play up to six games simultaneously. See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Pocket battles: Celts Vs Romans
description: Designed by Paolo Mori & Francesco Sirocchi.  As originally arted by Karim Chakroun.  Awards:  2010 JoTa Best 2-Player Board Game Nominee!
notes: Conversion by Balif.  Celts vs. Romans is the first in the ancient's line and also the first in the Pocket Battle series. Tiles represent troops and troops make up units in your army: just determine the size of the battle and create your own army from a pool of existing troops. Each tile hits on certain rolls, and some can only melee while others can shoot. Some tiles also have special traits which can affect their whole unit or their whole army. Armies fight in three sectors - the battlefield. The goal is to eliminate at least half the value of your opponent's army. See BGG and Z-Man Games for further information!

title: Pocogaligo 1862 and 1864
description: Designed by Robert B. McNair.  Artist Unknown, should you know please answer on ZT Forums.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for scenarios 15.3 and 15.7. The War Between The States near Hilton Head Island and Beaufort, South Carolina. See BGG for more information!

title: Poker v2
description: Designed by Jerome.  Graphics by Jerome.  Please feel free to use all graphics for your ZT Designs!
notes: Conversion by Jerome. This game box is meant to demonstrate how ZunTzu handles playing cards.  This is THE EXAMPLAR in understanding cards in ZT.

title: Polska 1939
description: Designed by Wojciech Zalewski. Map by Wojciech Zalewski.  Artist:  Arkadiusz Wrobel.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in Polish and English. Play the full Polish campaign. Map covers Polish territory in 1939 and supplies all Polish, German and Soviet forces that were involved in the first campaign of WW2. Additional Slovakian, Lithuanian and Romanian units also included. See BGG & Tactics & Strategy (Taktyka i Strategia) for more information!

title: Poltava 1709
description: Designed by Marco Campari. System by Wojciech Zalewski. Graphics by Adam Lapko, Damian Rozpędek, and Piotr Promiński. Map by Wojciech Zalewski and Piotr Promiński.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. On July 8, 1709, a battle took place near Poltava between the Swedes, commanded by King Charles XII, and the Russians, commanded by Tsar Peter the Great.  Charts in English and Polish. Game not listed at BGG.   See Taktyka i Strategia for more information!

title: Ponyri-Kursk: The Northern Pincers July 7 & 8, 1943
description: Designed by Paul Rohrbaugh. Graphics by Art Lupinacci and Robert Tunstall. Part of the Blood & Steel series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. A stand-alone Blood & Steel system game designed by Paul Rohrbaugh and is an extension of the highly successful Blood & Steel folio game on the battle of Kursk. See BGG & L2 Design Group for more information!

title: Port Arthur
description: Designed by Mark W. Miller.  Arted by Rich Banner aka Rich Banner).  A companion game with 'Tsushima.'  Which can be found on ZT2.
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson. Port Arthur is a strategic simulating the land campaign in Manchuria fought between Russia and Japan, 1904-05. Individual counters representing infantry divisions,and cavalry and artillery at lower levels, maneuver on a map depicting the lay of the land in Manchuria, with units engaging in combat while seeking national objectives. See BGG and FarFutures for more information!

title: Port Stanley
description: Designed by Albert C.E. Parker. Original graphics concepts by Thomas D. Ciampa. Cover art by Jan French. Map by Ina Clausen. Counters by Howard Bond. Published in Wargamer #28.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. This game was published in The Wargamer Magazine #28. It simulates the British land campaign to retake the Falklands from the Argentine forces in May and June 1982. More info at BGG .

title: Position Magnifique: Battle of Mars-la-tour, 1870
description: Designed by Hermann Luttmann.  Artists: Knut Grünitz, Dan Lamb and Brien J. Miller.  As originally seen in "Paper Wars Magazine."
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  The game requires the players to maintain supply lines, both to rally units that are shaken or low on ammo and to achieve the victory conditions. See BGG and Compass Games & Paper Wars for more information!

title: Power Grid
description:
Designed by Friedemann Friese.  As arted by Domonkos Bence, Antonio Dessì, Lars-Arne 'Maura' Kalusky, Prapach Lapamnuaysap and Harald Lieske.
Awards: 2004 Meeples Choice Award Winner +20 others (see BGG).
notes: Convertor Unknown.  If you know, please leave a message on the ZT Forums!   See who can supply the most cities with power. This is an older ZT1 ZTB as found in the "Zwever Collection." See BGG amd Rio Grande Games for more information!

title: Prague, the Battle of 1st Edition
description: Designed by Frank Chadwick.  Artist:  During this period of our hobby, artists were not always attributed. Should you know, please mention on ZT Forum!
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  A faithful rendition of GDWs Series 120 game.  The Battle of Prague follows the victories of Fredrick the Great's Army in 1757 during the Seven Years War. It recreates the battle fought just to the east of Prague between the Austrians and Prussians. See BGG and FarFutures for further information!

title: Prelude to Disaster
description: Designed by Henry Robinette. Original system design by John Schettler. Graphics by Rick Barber. Part of the Winter Storm series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Prelude to Disaster: The Soviet Spring Offensive - May 1942, is Volume No. 6 of the Winter Storm Campaign Series by Clash of Arms Games, originaly designed by John Schettler and has the same Basic Rules like Edelweiss and Last Victory.  Setup provided for Scenario 12.1 (Timoshenko Strikes!). See BGG and Clash of Arms Games (COA)for more information.

title: Princes of Florence, The - in English
description:
Designed by Wolfgang Kramer and Richard Ulrich.  Artwork by Arnaud Demaegd, Eckhard Freytag, Wolfgang Kramer, Mirco Paganessi, Lukas Siegmon, Richard Ulrich and Franz Vohwinkel.
Translated from Zuntzuniacos original ZTB.
notes: Conversion (translator) by Unknown.  If you know, please leave a message on the ZT Forums.  Attract artists and scholars while trying to become the most prestigious family in Florence. An older ZT1 ZTB found in the Zwever Collection.  Submitted by R. Peterson. See BGG , Rio Grande Games and Whikids for more information!

links.url: https://zuntzu.com/gameboxes/Rio Grande Games/Princes of Florence engl  translation.ztb

title: Príncipes de Florencia, Los - En español
description: Designed by Wolfgang Kramer and Richard Ulrich.  Artwork by Arnaud Demaegd, Eckhard Freytag, Wolfgang Kramer, Mirco Paganessi, Lukas Siegmon, Richard Ulrich and Franz Vohwinkel.
notes: Conversion by Zuntzuniacos.  Patrons and artists in 16th century Italy.  "Atrae a artistas y eruditos mientras intentas convertirte en la familia más prestigiosa de Florencia." An older ZT1 ZTB found in the Zwever Collection.  Submitted by R. Peterson. See BGG , Rio Grande Games and Whiz Kids for more information!

title: Puerto Rico - in English
description:
Designed by Andreas Seyfarth.  Artwork by Franz Vohwinkel.
Awards:  Over 20 awards - see BGG entry for full listing.

description:
Designed by Éric Grenier. Artwork by William J. Jhoslien. 

Awards:  2006 Charles S. Roberts Best DTP-Produced Boardgame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Quelques Arpents de Neige is a two-player regimental game with each player taking the side of either the French Empire or the British Empire. Both players have native allies to control and the French player can also control what's left of the Spanish Empire in North America. No setups provided. See BGG for more information.

title: Ra

title: Race for the Galaxy - Po Polsku
description:
Designed by Thomas Lehmann. Artwork by Martin Hoffmann, Claus Stephan. See BGG entry for full listing by language and version. Awards: Multiple awards winner - see BGG entry for full listing!
Copyright© 2007 (?) Publisher: Rio Grande Games + 18 more.
ZT Note:  We are still looking for the ZT1 English version (?)
notes: Conversion by Unknown, should you know please leave a message on the ZT Forum!  Race for the Galaxy gracze budują galaktyczne cywilizacje, grając kartami reprezentującymi światy lub techniczne i społeczne osiągnięcia. Dla 2-4 graczy. Pudełko z grą przedstawia układ ze wszystkimi kartami i elementami oraz dwie zakładki pomocy ułatwiające grę. Cały tekst jest w języku polskim. (In Race for the Galaxy, players build galactic civilizations by playing cards representing worlds or technical and social developments. For 2-4 players. The gamebox shows a layout with all cards and pieces and two help tabs to aid play. All of the text is in Polish.) See BGG and Rio Grande Games for more information! This older ZT1 ZTB was found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by F. Jordan.

title: Racławice 1794
description:
1st edition. Designed by Adam Niechwiej. Counters by Jacek Grzesiowski.  Map artist is unknown; should you know, please comment on ZT Forums (in Polish or English)!
Another excellent Polish game produced by Terry Gordon.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  Charts in English and Polish. The game "Racławice 1794" presents one of the most famous victories in the history of Poland.  The rules reflect fundamental aspects of the XVIII century battlefield, with the dominant linear formation. Gameplay is divided into 15 rounds. Setup provided for the historical scenario. See BGG and Strategemata for more information!

title: Raid on Saint Nazaire
description: Designed by Robert G. Markham and Mark Seaman.  Original graphics by Charles J. Kibler II and George Ira Parrish, Jr.  Awards: 1987 Charles S. Roberts Best World War II Board Game Winner & 1987 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargame Graphics Winner - see BGG for more . . .
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  This solitaire wargame simulates the March 28, 1942, British raid on the Nazi-occupied French port of St. Nazaire. In the first part of the game, the player moves the British boats and destroyer HMS Campbeltown (camouflaged as a German ship) to their landing areas, while determining the results of the many shots from the harbor defense guns. Upon landing, the remaining force tries to reach targets (sub pens, caissons, docked ships, supply tanks, etc.) and destroy them. The German guards are handled by the game system and arrive via random draw and placement and move by most direct route to the nearest British commando. As the game progresses, the German units get tougher and better organized. The game ends when either all British units are killed or escape and they score for the targets destroyed. See BGG and Avalon Hill and Markham Designs for further information.

title: Railroad Tycoon: The Boardgame
description:
Designed by Glenn Drover and Martin Wallace.  Artwork by Kurt Miller, Paul Niemeyer and David A. Oram.
Awards: 2006 Juego del Año Finalist; 2006 International Gamers Awards - General Strategy; Multi-player Nominee; 2006 Golden Geek Best Gamer's Board Game Nominee; 2006 Golden Geek Best Family Board Game Nominee; 2005 Meeples Choice Award Nominee!
ZT Note:  We are uncertain of Edition, please inform on the ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  If you know leave a message on ZT Forums! Build your budding railroad network into a vast empire. Rail and New City tiles are terrain.  Enable terrain editing to add them to the map.   Train minis can be flipped over to allow for more angles of rotation (double right click). See BGG and Eagle-Gryphon Games for more information! This an older ZT1 ZTB found in the Geralt Collection by R. Peterson.

title: Raphia, the Battle of 1st Edition
description: Designed by the famous Marc W. Miller.  Artist:  During this period of our wargame history, artists were not always attributed.  Should you know, please, post on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  A faithful conversion of the 1st Edition.  Another GDW Series 120 game.  Concerning the 217 BC battle of Raphia, which used Elephants. See BGG and FarFutures for further information!

title: Rattus
description:
Designed by Ase Berg & Henrick Berg.  
Winner of 2011 Luca Best Family Game AND Golden Geek Best Family Board Game!
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  A game of the 'Black Death' Under attack by the Plague, can you do better than your neighbors? See BGG and White Goblin Games for further information!

title: Rebel Sabers
description:
Designer: Richard Berg, George Deutsch
Map Graphics: Doug Chafee, Dave LaForce, Colleen O'Malley
Zun Tzu Counters: Mitch King
notes: Conversion by Mitch King. Rebel Sabers: Civil War Cavalry Battles is a game in the Great Battles of the American Civil War series designed by Richard Berg, originator of this regimental game system with Terrible Swift Sword in 1976.  The game scale varies between 120 and 180 yards per hex, 50 or 100 man strength points and 20 to 30 minute game turns, depending on the battle.  This game covers four battles: Kelly's Ford, Brandy Station, Trevaillians Station and the cavalry fighting at Gettysburg.  The Gettysburg cavalry field map joins to 2nd Edition maps in Terrible Swift Sword, not included in this game box.  The game box uses the counters created by Mitch King.  See BGG and Armchair Brigade for more details.  One player must own TSR's Rebel Sabers to use this game box.

title: Rebels and Redcoats III
description: Designed by Christopher Cummins.  Using original art by Emanuel Gottlieb Leutze (May 24, 1816 - July 18, 1868).
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Covers American Revolutionary War Battles of White Plains-Harlem Heights-Kings Mountain-Stony Point-Long Island-Trenton-Princeton. See BGG and Decision Games (DG) for more information!

title: Red Devil's
description: Design by John Butterfield; Graphics by Redmond Simonsen; The British 1st Airborne Division in the Battle of Arnhem. Part 1 of 3 of the Paratroop issue in S&T #77.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. Red Devils Plus is optimized for ZunTzu with charts and units already set up to play. The Turn Record is loaded with the reinforcement schedule and ZunTzu's terrain feature is used to mark the Polish drop zones in secret. Rules are included in a separate pdf file. The game was included as part of the Paratroop trilogy in issue 77 of Strategy & Tactics. Red Devils represents the battle of Arnhem where the British 1st Airborne Division dropped as part of Operation Market-Garden in September 1944. See DG for further information!  Also see BGG for S&T #77 .  . . This is a ZIP file, please download and Unzip for ZTB and other items!

title: Red Dragon Rising: The Coming War with China
description:
Designed by Bruce Costello, (Ty Bomba?).
Graphics by Nicolas Eskubi and Joe Youst.
Awards: 2008 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-WW2 era Board Game Winner; 2008 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-WW2 era Board Game Nominee; 2008 Charles S. Roberts Best Magazine-Published Boardgame Nominee.
As first seen in Strategy & Tactics #250.
notes: Conversion by J. David.  Red Dragon Rising: The Coming War With China (RDR), is a strategic-level investigation, with operational undertones, of the possibilities inherent in the first 30-or-so days of a hypothetical war between the Peoples Republic of China and a US-led counter-alliance. See BGG and Decision Games ( DG ) for more information! An older ZT1 ZTB found in the Geralt Collection.  Submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Red Dragon, Blue Dragon: The Huaihai 1948-49
description: Designed by Earl Dixon.  Arted by Gavin Hu, and Mark Mahaffey.
notes: Conversion by David Jones.  This showdown determined that the Nationalist forces of Jiang Jieshi (Chiang Kai-Shek) would be driven from the mainland into exile in Taiwan. It was the culmination of 20 years of on-again-off-again civil war between the Nationalists and the Communists. See BGG and ATO for further information!

This one covers the period June 1950 to late January 1951 at a scale of 18 km per hex. Charts in English and Chinese. Setups provided for all scenarios, with scenario 4 being the default. See BGG and War Drum Games Facebook page, for more information.

title: Red Star/White Eagle, The Russo-Polish War, 1920
description:
Designed by Dave Williams. Art direction by Paul Richard Banner (& Rodger B. MacGowan?).  Historically, this conflict is similar to the current Ukraine/Russian War.
Update Note: (1/10/26) Fixed Naming error, all prior downloads do work!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for all scenarios. Russo-Polish War of 1920. Three scenarios and a campaign game chart the course of the Bolshevik invasion of Poland and the great Polish victory on the banks of the Vistula. This regiment-brigade-division level game is scaled at one week turns and 14 mile hexes. Intended for ages 12 to adult. For more information, see BGG also see FarFutures.net .

title: Red Sun Black Cross (with Escort Fleet)
description: Includes both the RSBC game and its Escort Fleet expansion. RSBC designed by Shunichi Takanishi; EF designed by Makoto Fukada. System designed by Daisuke Seto and Makoto Fukada. Graphics by Makoto Fukada and Makoto Sekine.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English and 日本語 (Japanese). The setting for the game is that Germany won WW2 (conquered Europe) due to Japan not attacking the USA and we both stayed neutral while Japan picked up territorial concessions. Now it is 1948 and Germany and Japan are about to fight it out for control of the Indian subcontinent. The USA is on Japan’s side in the conflict. Default scenario is the linked RSBC/EF Grand Campaign. Setups also provided for the RSBC campaign and the EF "Bloody Ocean" scenario. See BGG here and here for more information.

title: REDS! 1ere
description: Designed by Ted Racier.  As arted by Rodger B. MacGowan and Mark Simonitch.  Awards:  2002 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Boardgame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by Provence. Vous devez posséder le jeu pour le télécharger.  You must have the original game to download it. Reds! is a two-player wargame covering these dramatic events from August 1918 to the start of 1921, when the last organized opposition to Red rule outside the far east was destroyed. At least one player must own a physical copy of game - to download and play! See BGG and GMT for more information!

title: Remember Gordon
description: Designed by Peter Bertram.  During this period of our hobby, artists were not always attributed.  Should you know, please post on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Remember Gordon! The Battle of Omdurman and bonus, The Fall of Khartoum. This is a simulation game of the final battle in Great Britain's two-year campaign to reassert her presence in the Sudan (1896-1898). Played with square army tokens on a hexagonal map players battle through the campaign game or the historical scenario gaining victory points by eliminating the opponent's forces. See BGG for further information!

title: Renaissance of Infantry
description: Designed by Albert A. Nofi.  As originally arted by Redmond Askel Simonsen.  As originally seen in S&T magazine #22.
notes: Conversion by J. Patterson. Renaissance of Infantry Tactical Warfare 1250A.D. - 1550A.D. See BGG & DG for more information!

title: Renaissance of Infantry 1250 to 1550 AD w PanzerBlitz Mini Game  PLUS+
description:
Designed by Albert Nofi. Art by Redmond Simonsen.


Renaissance of Infantry PLUS; Twenty scenarios representing historical battles circa 1200 to 1525 as first presented in Strategy & Tactics issue #22. 


BONUS: PanzerBlitz mini game included!


S&T Issue #22 presented a PanzerBlitz preview and that's included here as well.  Germans v Russians in 1944. It opens up ready to play, complete with backprinted counters, all charts and tables, and--again with a tip of the hat to Maxfin-- three pages of rules accessible on ZunTzu's tabs. These were the early days of SPI when physical components were limited; black and white maps, uncut counters and folio printed rules. But the designs were good and each S&T issue game was eagerly anticipated. Here's your chance to go back a half century and play some of them on ZunTzu!
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. Gamebox optimized for ZunTzu play. (See the ZT on the icon pic.) New flip side counters, twenty scenarios with setups ready to play, charts and tables accessible on the main screen, fortifications "locked in" as Terrain features, 3D effects on pieces, and, to lessen unit crowding, a 10% enlarged map...it's even colorized. Naturally, as a PLUS box, the rules are included. They're in a separate PDF file AND --using Maxfin's innovative technique--they are also incorporated into every scenario as tabs. Easy referencing! See BGG and DG for more information! ** This PLUS box is a zip file; download and unzip to access the gamebox and extras! **

title: Republic of Rome PLUS
description:
Designed by Don Greenwood, Richard Berthold, Robert Haines.
As arted by Dave Dobyski, Charles Kibler, Kurt Miller, George Ira Parrish, Jr., Patrick Turner and Mark Poole.

Awards:  1990 Origins Awards Best Pre-20th Century Boardgame Winner; 1990 James F. Dunnigan Award for Playability and Design Nominee; 1990 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargaming Graphics Nominee; 1990 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee.
notes: Conversion by D. Laufle.  Original AH classic of Senatorial Intrigue.  An older lost ZT1 ZTB found by R. Peterson. See BGG & Avalon Hill for more information! ** Please download & unzip for ZTB! **

title: Return to Europe - in English & 日本語
description: Designed by Daisuke Sato. Graphics by Makoto Fukada. Third game set in the Red Sun Black Cross alternative history timeline.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  In the ‘history’ of RTE, Europe has been conquered by the Germans, and the USA is coming to save the day (again). Europe has been broken up into many minor provinces with Germanic sounding names and spellings, including many of their own combat units.  Charts in English and Japanese. Setup provided for the full campaign. See BGG for more information.

title: Revolt on Antares Ver.1.0 (New artwork)
description:
Designed by Tom Moldvay.  Original artists: Jeff Dee, David S. LaForce, Erol Otus, James Paul "Jim" Roslof and Bill Willingham.
Updated Maps & Counters by Ed Messina, using his Vassal module!
notes: Conversion by E, Sprague. Play this game with updated graphics by E. Messina. Rebels vs. Terrans on the planet of Antares. See BGG and Decision Games (DG) for more information!

title: Riachuelo's Naval Battle
description:
Designed by Antonio Marcelo. Map and counters by Antonio Marcelo.
A Brazilian title, translated for the English market.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. The Riachuelo’s Naval Battle is a war game for two players, that reproduces the riverine naval battle of June 11, 1865, where, during the War of the Triple Alliance (known in Brazil as the Paraguayan War). In this battle the admiral Barroso achieved an important victory, destroying a great part of the Paraguayan fleet. See BGG and Wargame Downloads for more information.

title: Right Fierce & Terrible:  Sluys 1340
description:
Designed by Jeremy White, graphics  Mark Mahaffey!  The first Naval Battle of the Hundred Years War.
As done by Against the Odds Magazine #34.
notes: Conversion by Dave Jones.  With permission of ATO and the artist.  Right Fierce & Terrible simulates the battle in 1340 between English King Edward III and a French fleet assembled to carry King Philip VI’s invasion across the English Channel. See BGG and ATO for further information!

title: Rio Grande: The Battle of Valverde
description: Designed by Richard H. Berg. Map graphics by Mark Simonitch. Published in Strategy & Tactics #143.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Rio Grande is a mid complexity tactical level wargame, covering the battle of Valverde, fought in New Mexico Territory, on February 21, 1862, between the Union forces (and New Mexico volunteers) led by Col. Edward Canby and the Confederate Army of New Mexico (mostly Texas troopers and Arizona volunteers) . . . The game highlights cavalry vs. infantry fighting. For more info, see BGG and Decision Games .

title: River of Death
description:
Designer: Richard Berg
Artists: Rodger B. MacGowan, Mark Simonitch & Joe Youst
1999 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargame Graphics Winner
1999 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargame Graphics Nominee
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  This is a regimental level Great Battles of the Civil War game featuring the Battle of Chickamauga from September 18 to 20, 1863.  The battle represented the last great Confederate victory of the American Civil War.  The game uses 50 men per strength point, 140 yard hexes, 50 foot elevation differences and 20 minute game turns. See BGG and GMT Games for more information.  One of the players in the game MUST own a physical copy of GMT Game's River of Death to use this game box.

title: Rivets PLUS, 2nd Edition
description:
Designed by Robert Taylor.  Arted by Russell Ansley and Brian Wilson.

Microgame #5 in the Metagaming Microgames series.
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  A really fun game about AI! Rivets is a tactical level science fiction game of robotical warfare in the 22nd century. The players choose their robot armies, program them, and maneuver them to destroy the computer complex that controls the enemy's robots. See BGG for more information!

title: Rivoli 1797
description: Designed by José Luis Arcón. Artwork by Carmen Sánchez. Part of the Battles of the Revolution and the Empire series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in English. Setups provided for both the basic and advanced games. For more info, see BGG .

title: Road to Richmond: The Peninsular Campaign, May-July 1862
description: Designed by Joseph Angiolillo.  Graphics by Redmond Askel Simonsen.  As first introduced in S&T #60.
notes: Conversion by D. Deitch.  Road to Richmond is an extra Blue and Gray Civil War Quad game, first published in Strategy & Tactics magazine #60. Also released in Folio format See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Road to Richmond: The Peninsular Campaign, May-July 1862
description: Designed by Joseph Angiolillo.  Graphics by Redmond Askel Simonsen.  As first introduced in S&T #60.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. Road to Richmond optimized for ZunTzu with all charts and units set up and ready to go. This gamebox has backprinted counters, redone reinforcement tracks, a "floating" CRT, and two versions of the mapboard: one with North facing up (landscape mode) and the other with West facing up (portrait mode; as printed in S&T 60). The rules are included in a separate pdf file with all known errata incorporated. The game is part of the Blue and Gray series and represents the battles fought in the 1862 Peninsula Campaign while McClellan was changing his base to the James River. This is a ZIP file - please download and unzip for the ZTB and more!  Please SEE! See BGG and DG for further information!

title: Road to the Rhine
description: Designed by Frank Chadwick. Art direction by Paul Richard Banner.  Artwork by Rodger B. MacGowan.  As of 7/22/2022, Compass Games has a new version in development?  Should you know, please feel free to update on ZT Forums!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  Fully setup to play. This is a simulation of the post-Normandy campaigns from September 1st, 1944 to April 1945 on the West front. The game covers the initial attempts by the Allies to maintain the pace of their advance in the face of a rapidly deteriorating logistical situation, the German recovery culminating in the Battle of the Bulge, and the final Allied drive across the Rhine. See BGG , FarFutures and Compass Games (?) for more information!

title: Road to Washington
description: Designed by James Murphy. Map graphics by Ronald D. Roundy.  A highly touted game system; considered by some as a scholastic achievement (better than GBCW?).
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Includes all tactical and operational maps. Setups provided for scenarios 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 8A, 12, and 12A. I encourage you to double-check each scenario you begin, as the way they are presented in the rule book makes them very challenging to prepare. I have made the following enhancements to the published game: * Added a turn record track to make it possible to set up reinforcements prior to play. * Added markers to indicate day of arrival for each stack of reinforcements. * Added operational group displays. * Added markers to show the boundaries for a scenario. * Added hex numbers to the map (via my Vassal module for the game). * Changed the color of water features on the map from green to blue so that they stand out better. See BGG for more information.

title: Roads to Gettysburg
description:
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski
Artwork: Charles Kibler
Cover Art: Keith Rocco
 Awards & Honors:
    1994 Origins Awards Best Pre-20th Century Boardgame Winner 
ZunTzu Counter Art: DGruehn
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  Roads to Gettysburg is third game in the Great Battles of the Civil War series.  This covers the 1863 Invasion of Pennsylvania Campaign culminating Meade's defeat of Lee at the Battle of Gettysburg.  This is the original Avalon Hill 1994 version, not the Multi-Man Publishing reprint.  The counters have been updated using DGruehn's excellent artwork he posted on BGG.  Gruehn's counters have been updated to match the original AH values and to correct typos.  The game box includes setups for all six scenarios.  See BGG & Avalon Hill for more details.  One player must own Avalon Hill's "Roads to Gettysburg" to use this game box.

title: Robert the Bruce v1.1
description: Designed by Kenneth Clark. Graphics by Stewart Cordiner.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. This game deals with the Scots Wars of Independence in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, on land and sea. The general objective is to be crowned King of the Scots. There are five basic scenarios. Setup provided for Scenario 3. See BGG for more information.

title: Robo Rally - Po Polsku
description:
Designed by Richard Garfield. Artwork by Peter Bergting, Bob Carasca, Phil Foglio, Daniel Gelon and others. See BGG entry for full listing by language and version. Awards: Multiple awards winner - see BGG entry for full listing!
Copyright© Wizards of the Coast, 1994 (?) Publisher: Wizards of the Coast, Avalon Hill, and others.
notes: W RoboRally każdy z graczy steruje innym robotem w wyścigu przez niebezpieczną halę fabryczną. Dla 2 do 8 graczy. Plansze można łączyć na kilka sposobów, aby dostosować je do różnej liczby graczy, a wyścigi mogą być tak długie lub tak krótkie, jak sobie tego życzą gracze. (In RoboRally players each control a different robot in a race through a dangerous factory floor. For 2 to 8 players. Boards can be combined in several ways to accommodate different player counts and races can be as long or as short as players desire.) This ZTB was found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by F. Jordan. See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information!

title: Rolica et Vimeiro,  1808 1of2
description:
Designed by Frédéric Bey.  Artist Pascal da Silva.
This is Rolica . . .
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. ROLICA AND VIMEIRO 1808 is a new module of the Jours de Gloire series, including two battles of the 1808 Campaign of Portugal (Junot against Wellesley). See BGG and Canons en Carton for more information!

title: Rolica et Vimeiro,  1808 2of2
description:
Designed by Frédéric Bey.  Artist Pascal da Silva.
This is Vimeiro . . .
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. ROLICA AND VIMEIRO 1808 is a new module of the Jours de Gloire series, including two battles of the 1808 Campaign of Portugal (Junot against Wellesley). See BGG and Canons en Carton for more information!

title: Rome, Inc.: From Augustus to Diocletian
description: Designed by Philip Jelley.  Artist: Mark Mahaffey.  As originally introduced in ATO Magazine #53.  You must own the game to play (as of 2021).
notes: Conversion by E. Gallego.  With permission from ATO & Artist: Mark Mahaffey.  You must own the game to play (as of 2021). "ROME, INC. - From Augustus to Diocletian" by designer Philip Jelley is a solitaire wargame of the Roman Empire from Augustus in 27 BCE to Diocletian in 286 CE. See BGG & ATO for more information!

title: Rommel at Bay V1.2
description: Designed by Vance von Borries. Box art by Rodger B. MacGowan. Map by Kevin Zucker. Counters by Joyce Gusner. Part of the Battles for North Africa series.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setups provided for both scenarios. Rommel at Bay is an operational level simulation of the World War II Allied offensive in southern Tunisia which took place in mid-March 1943. Located here were the main Axis fortifications defending Tunisia, fortifications nearly as formidable as those at Alamein. Had the German-Italian army succeeded in defending, the war in North Africa would have been lengthened and perhaps Allied command would have changed again. This update features the following enhancements: * Counter resolution upgraded to 400 dpi. * Free-floating charts. * Starting units for Scenarios 1 and 2 placed on the map. * Added the small marker sheet from Decision at Kasserine. More info at BGG .

title: Rommel in North Africa
description:
North Africa campaign, 1941-42.
Design by Jon Southard.  As arted by Stephen Crane, Richard A. Johnson and Kevin Wilkins.
This might be from Wargamer Magazine #51 - but unsure?
notes: Conversion by federico67.  The Desert Sere, serene, eternal, the Western Desert stretches across North Africa. Here, Rommel - perhaps the greatest of Germany's generals - marshalled Italian troops and powerful German panzer forces to sweep the desert in brilliant blitzkrieg. See BGG1 and BGG2 for more information!  Please see ZT Forums to answer . . .

title: Russian Civil War 1918-1922
description: Designed by the famed James F. Dunnigan.  Artist: Redmond Askel Simonsen.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Part of SPI's Power Politics series, the historical simulation of the military and political conflict of 1918-1921 which abolished the Czarist regime and created the foundation of the Soviet Union. Each player controls one or more factions drawn from the revolutionary, counter-revolutionary, nationalist and interventionist forces which historically participated. For this reason, players may even find it advantageous to attack their own forces. Victory depends first on the side one wants (either revolutionary or counter-revolutionary) winning the war and second on being the player most successful defeating the forces of the losing side. See BGG and DG for further information!

Is there a World War I? title: Singapore PLUS
description: Designed by Charles Kamps and David James Ritchie.   Art by Jerry Tiritilli, Ivor M. Janci and David S. LaForce (all versions).  As first seen in S&T #96.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. A massive rework here and a beautiful display of what ZunTzu can do. The Singapore game in S&T 96 had gorgeous art but a strange layout that put a blowup of Singapore Island at the top of the Malay peninsula and at right angles to it! This game box corrects that with a whole new presentation that eliminates redundant charts and uses the space to put Singapore where it belongs...at the bottom tip of the peninsula and with North pointing up. (Then all the text was reworked so you don't have to read anything sideways.) All the tables and charts have been recolored to match the color of the terrain the chart affects; a green line on the CRT for jungle; a yellow line for beach, etc. The counters are completely new, not scans. The optional rules are "ZunTzu optimized" by using the terrain feature to overlay sections of the map with the optional rules and features. There's really too much to describe here. As always with a Plus box, the rules are included. In this case an annotated scan from the magazine, a clean copy with errata incorporated, and a rules summary for easy reference. The game itself was one of the better ones to come out of TSR's time at the helm of S&T. It has a nice list of options to explore the sad "what ifs" of Britain's humiliating loss of Singapore. See BGG and DG for more information! This is a ZIP file, please unzip to see the ZTB and extras!

notes: Konwersja przez nieznany. Steruj rasami stworzeń o specjalnych mocach, aby zdobywać relikwie i walczyć z potworami w tym podziemnym świecie. Chociaż Small World Underground jest grywalny sam w sobie, wydawca zaleca, aby gracze zapoznali się ze Small World. Zakładki ZunTzu są po polsku, ale komponenty gry są po angielsku. See BGG and Days of Wonder for more information! Found in the Geralt Collection.  As submitted by F. Jordan.

title: Smolensk 20 With Expansion Kit v1.0
description:
Designed by Alan Emrich, Map Graphics by Chris Magoun.
Russia 1812 - Retreat Before Moscow
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett "Smolensk 20 is based on a trap sprung from August 16 to 19 during Napoleon’s Russian campaign in 1812 where the Russian ‘scorched earth’ retreat almost ended in a decisive pitched battle. One player commands the French army of Napoleon, while the other leads the (Russian) Anti-French forces under Barclay do Tolly." Second of the Russia 20 games in VPG's Napoleonic 20 series. The Expansion kit is integrated and loads by default. See BGG and VPG for more information!

title: Snapshot
description: Designed by Marc W. Miller.  As arted (all editions) by Rich Banner, Jennell Jaquays and Chris White.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  Snapshot: Close Combat aboard Star ships in the Far Future. This is the Second game in aiding Traveller RPG players to use the RPG rules. See BGG and FarFutures.net for rules and more!

title: Soldier King
description:
Designed by Frank Chadwick.  
During this period of our wargaming history, artists were not attributed.  Should you, know, please make a notice on ZT Forums,
notes: Conversion by R Peterson. Soldier King is a game for 2-4 players covering a War of succession in a leaderless empire.  This is an early development of the highly regarded game " A House Divided. " See BGG and FarFuture for more information!

title: Soldier of the Queen: Isandlwana
description: Designed by Richard Harvey Berg.  Graphics by Kristine L. Bartyzel, Ivor M. Janci, John Meyers, Keith Parkinson & Stephen D. Sullivan.  As originally presented in S&T #95.  NOTE this box only includes Isandlwana.
notes: Conversion by S Rugge.  In Isandhlwana, the Zulu player wins if he eliminates all British units before he himself loses 14, otherwise the British player wins; the game has no set time limit... it is played until one player or the other has achieved their victory conditions. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Soldiers of the Queen PLUS
description:
Designed by Richard Berg. Published in Strategy & Tactics no. 95.
This ZTB Includes rules and incorporates errata, with same little graphic adjustment.  Please leverage "Open Scenario" to find all assets!
notes: Conversion by Maaaax. Battle of Isandhlwana 1879 & Battle of Omdurman 1898. Soldiers of the Queen is actually two separate colonial battle games that use the same game system: Isandhlwana, 1879 and Omdurman, 1898. The game was originally published in Strategy & Tactics magazine (#95). See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Solferino & San Martino 24 Giugno 1859
description: Includes the companion game San Martino 24 Giugno 1859. Both designed by Massimilliano Bertuzzi and R. Buschi. Artist's unknown, if you know please leave a ZT Forum post!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Big game over the battle of Solferino. Battalion/squadron level, 1700 counters, two maps. Linking with San Martino 24 Giugno 1859 (included in ZTB). Charts in Italian and English. With setup for the combined battles. See BGG1 (Solferino) and BGG2 (San Martino) for more information!

title: Solferino 24 Juin 1859 - French
description:
Designed by Jean-Pierre Défieux.  Artist unknown, should you know - please leave a message on ZT Forums!
Published by Jeux Descartes.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Charts in French. Livret - Jeu défi Nº4 Rules in French only.  Game is played in 17 turns. The first two represent 2 hours of real time and the other 15 only one hour each.  Includes a big folding mapboard representing the battlefield and 81 die-cut counters . See BGG and Jeux Descartes fro more information!

title: Some Poles Apart, The Battle of the Westerpatte
description:
Designed by Paul Rorhbaugh.  As arted by Craig Grando.
Some Poles Apart is the second game in the Pocket Battle Games series from LPS, Inc., released to promote Against the Odds (ATO).  Many other free 'post-card' games distributed by ATO Magazine . . .
notes: Conversion by federico67.  A ZT1 game found by R. Peterson. Some Poles Apart takes a close look at a fascinating and almost unknown action from the opening days of WWII, when a small group of Polish troops earned full "Honors of War" from the Nazis for an amazing defensive stand they made in a Polish military storehouse on Westerplatte, a peninsula in the then Free City of Gdańsk. See BGG and ATO Mgazine for more information!

title: Source of the Nile PLUS+
description:
Designed by Ross Maker and David A. Wesely.  Art by Dale A. Sheaffer.  New art by Massimo Finocchiaro (aka Maaaax)!
Awards: 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-Twentieth Century Game Winner & Nominee.  1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Amateur Game Winner & Nominee.
notes: Conversion by Massimo Finocchiaro (aka Maaaax) . Game of African Exploration in the 19th Century This version for ZunTzu has been specially redesigned to eliminate the need for written annotations. The graphics have been completely changed, because it was, in my opinion, the weak point of an otherwise very interesting game.

title: Soviet Dawn: The Russian Civil War 1918-1921.
description:
Designed by Darin A. Leviloff.  As arted by Tim Allen, Knut Grünitz, and Rodger B. MacGowan.  As first seen in C3i no. 27.
A new game concerning the Russian Civil War.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Soviet Dawn brings Darin Leviloff’s novel States of Siege(TM) game system (introduced in VPG’s Israeli Independence) back for a much larger storytelling adventure covering the Russian Civil War from 1918 to 1921. With several enemy "Fronts" converging on Moscow, the fate of the revolution and the prestige of international communism rests on your ability to manage and resolve every crisis that the "Whites" can assail you with. See BGG , RBM Studios ( C3i ) Magazine and VPG for more information!

title: Space Hulk: Death Angel - Po Polsku & English
description: Designed by Corey Konieczka.  Graphics by Matthew Bradbury, Kevin Chin, Victor Perez-Corbella, Daniel Xiao and six others (see BGG for more), Awards: 2011 Golden Geek Best Card Game Nominee & 2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Science-Fiction or Fantasy Board Wargame Nominee!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  If you know, please leave a message on ZT Forums  A cooperative game where players attempt to clean out an infestation of hostile aliens from a derelict spaceship.  Presented in English & Polish! See BGG and Fantasy Flight Games (FFG) for more information! As found in Geralt Collection & submitted by R. Peterson.

Designed by Corey Konieczka.  Graphics by Matthew Bradbury, Kevin Chin, Victor Perez-Corbella, Daniel Xiao and six others (see BGG for more), Awards: 2011 Golden Geek Best Card Game Nominee & 2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Science-Fiction or Fantasy Board Wargame Nominee!

title: Spanish Civil War Battles: Vol.2 - Guadalajara & Penarroya
description: Designed by Perry Moore.  Graphics by Larry Hoffman & Joseph Youst.  As first seen in S&T #219.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Includes the Guadalajara: The Italians Strike for Madrid & Penarroya: The Last Gasp. See BGG and DG for further information!

title: Spanish Civil War, The 1936 to 1939
description:
Designed by Javier Romero.  As arted by Charles J. Kibler II & Rodger B. MacGowan.
Awards:  2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-Napoleonic to Pre-World War 2 Era Board Wargame Nominee & 2010 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-Napoleonic to Pre-World War 2 Era Board Wargame Winner!!!
notes: Conversion by Maaaax. If you are fan of this campaign - this is a must see! Award wining game on the Spanish Civil War 1936-1939! Game scales are Column-Brigade-Division, with monthly turns. This ZTB does not contains rules.  Rules and Playbook are needed to play the game.  At least one player must own a physical copy to download & play ZTB. See BGG & GMT for information!

title: Spanish Eagles
description:
Designed by Stephen C. Jackson and Brien Miller.
Artist: Brien Miller.  With permission by Compass Games and artist Brien Miller
notes: Conversion by D. Jones.  An Eagles of the Empire series games.  Featuring two complete battles of the Peninsular War, Talavera and Albuera, each with an alternate set-up possibility. See BGG and Compass Games for more information!

title: Spartacus: A Game of Blood and Treachery V.02
description:
Designed by Aaron Dill, John Kovaleski and Sean Sweigart.  Artwork by Charles Woods.
Awards: 2013 Spiel der Spiele Hit für Experten Recommended and 2013 Golden Geek Best Thematic Board Game Nominee!
Nice 3D minis included in ZTB.  Uniquely presented in BOTH Polish and English!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  Each player takes on the role of Dominus, head of a rising house in the ancient Roman city of Capua. Each house is competing for Influence to gain the favor of Rome. Through a combination of political schemes and glorious battles on the arena sands your house will rise in fame and stature. See BGG and GF9 (Gale Force 9 Games)!

title: Sphactirie (425 av. j.-c BC in English) in French
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey as arted by Christophe Camilotte and Pascal da Silva.  As first seen Vae Victis No. 95.
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  Should you know this Author, please contact ZT Forums!  Sfacteria (425 BC) is a two-player wargame on land and naval battles of Pylos and Sphacteria, during the first phase of the Peloponnesian War.  See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for further information!

title: Spies!
description: Designed by Lenny Glynn and John Prados.  Original graphics by Redmond Askel Simonsen.  Awards: 1981 Charles S. Roberts Best Twentieth Century Game Nominee.
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Spies is a game of espionage and intrigue for up to five players, set in the turbulent European era of 1933-1939. You control the secret service of one of the major powers of that era - Germany, Italy, Russia, France, and Britain - in the constant struggle to gather your opponent's secrets and return them safely to your own capital while protecting your own country's secrets. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Sportiv ® Football Edition - En français
description:
Designed and arted by Tony Leoni.
By kind permission of the author for non-commercial use.
notes: Conversion by Tony Leoni.  Football (soccer) card game. See BGG for rules and further information!

title: Squad Leader 2nd+ Edition
description:
Designed by the famous John Hill.  As originally arted by A. Richard Hamblen, Rodger B. MacGowan and W. Scott Moores.  Developed by Arthur Goodwin.
Awards:  2003 Origins Awards Hall of Fame Inductee.  1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Nominee.  1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Game Winner.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  Want to see the game that started ASL?  Unlike Vassal, this is a faithful rendition of John Hill's game.  To this day, Avalon Hill owns the rights to this historical wargame! See BGG , Avalon Hill and MMP for more information!

title: Squad Leader 2nd+ Edition BIG Version
description:
Designed by the famous John Hill.  As originally arted by A. Richard Hamblen, Rodger B. MacGowan and W. Scott Moores.  Developed by Arthur Goodwin.
Awards:  2003 Origins Awards Hall of Fame Inductee.  1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Nominee.  1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Game Winner.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  Unlike the prior version, this has double sized hexes to help with counter congestion. See BGG , Avalon Hill and MMP for more information!

description:
Designed by John Hill.  Artwork by Rodger B. MacGowan.
Awards: 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Twentieth Century Game Nominee, 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Graphics and Physical Systems Winner, 	
1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Graphics and Physical Systems Nominee,
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  What 'Squad Leader' did for  tactical infantry combat. 'Cross of Iron' does for armoured combat. See BGG , Avalon Hill and MMP for more information!

description: Designed by John Hill. Artwork by Rodger B. MacGowan. Awards: 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Twentieth Century Game Nominee, 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Graphics and Physical Systems Winner, 1978 Charles S. Roberts Best Graphics and Physical Systems Nominee,
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson. What 'Squad Leader' did for tactical infantry combat. 'Cross of Iron' does for armoured combat. BIG Hex version, with double sized hexes to aide in hex congestion. See BGG , A valon Hill and MMP for more information!

title: St Nazaire 1942
description: As originally seen in Encart-jeu VaeVictis n°73.  An older green-list ZT1 ZTB. Found by Jerome!  Any further information is welcomed . . . Please, use the ZT forum for more information!
notes: Conversion: Unknown. A french translation of Raid On Saint Nazaire, as published in VaeVictis #73 (?), this is not the original Avalon Hill version. See Vae Vitctis for more information!

title: Stalin's Tanks: Armor Battles on the Eastern Front
description:
Designed by Roger Damon.  Originally arted by Trace Hallowell and Ben Ostrander. New map and counters by Alois Schimmerlos 2014.
MicroHistory game #3.
ZT Folk, this is #700 hosted on our site - a true celebration!
notes: Conversion by Eric Sprague. Tactical wargame of WWII battles between Russia and Germany on the Eastern Front.  This game is like a lite-Panzerblitz in a pocket-sized format. A double sided reference sheet (also by Schimmerlos) is also included. See BGG for more information! ZT Folk, this is #700 hosted on our site - a true celebration!

links.url: https://zuntzu.com/gameboxes/Metagaming/Stalin's Tanks_ Armor Battles on the Eastern Front.ztb

title: Stalingrad '42 (1st Printing) PLUS+
description:
Designed and arted by Mark Simonitch (GMT staff artist).
Awards:
2019 Golden Geek Best Wargame Nominee
2019 Charles S. Roberts:  Best World War 2 Era Board Wargame Nominee; Best Original Box Cover Art Nominee; Best Board Wargame Rules Nominee
notes: Conversion by Maaaax. At least one player must own the game to download. Stalingrad ‘42 is a division-level game on the Axis 1942 summer offensive towards Stalingrad and the Caucasus. Historically, this epic struggle lasted for 6 months and saw the Axis armies reach the Volga and the Caucasus Mountains. But Soviet resistance stiffened and final victory eluded the German army at Stalingrad and in the Caucasus. Don't forget to leverage the ZT UIC for senarios etc. See BGG and regulary check GMT Games for support and updates!

title: Stalingrad 1st Edition: 1963
description: Designed by our hobby founder: Mr. Charles S. Roberts, along with Lindsey Shultz and Thomas N. Shaw.  Unfortunately, during this period of our hobby, artists were not always attributed.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  A Faithful rendition of THE earliest game concerning the War between Germany and Soviet Union during WW2.  A must see for new game developers. Rules NOT included.  See ZT Bill's/J. Cooper version - also on this site! See BGG and Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Stalingrad v1.1
description: Designed by our hobby founder: Mr. Charles S. Roberts, along with Lindsey Shultz and Thomas N. Shaw.  Unfortunately, during this period of our hobby, artists were not always attributed.  NOTE:  This a has updated graphics by the incomparable John Cooper!
notes: Conversion by Bill Barrett All map errors have been fixed and I re-oriented many of the placenames and charts to make it more "screen friendly".   I also removed most of the gradient fills from the counters (I'm sure they look great when printed, but they were rather grainy in ZunTzu), implemented a nice, rounded corner mask and upped the resolution by four times (to 1200dpi). Despite all that, the gamebox is 5mb lighter. There are 18 different 'scenarios' included - basically these are optimum setups for the Russians, figured out by expert players over the last 45 years. And once again, many thanks to John Cooper for his excellent artwork! See BGG and Avalon Hill for further information!

title: Stalingrad: A Walk in Hell
description: Designed by Mark H. Walker.  Graphics: Unknown.
notes: Conversion by D. Deitch.  Platoon-level simulation of the battle in Stalingrad with the city and nearby ground divided into areas. Players use cards to rally, refit, fire, and move their units, area by area. See BGG and Armchair Magazine for further information!

title: Stamford Bridge & A Hill Near Hastings
description: Two games from Tom Russell's 'Shields & Swords' system designed by Tom Russell (Amabel Holland?).  ZT Update Note: Is this Game Card, accurate?  Please leave a message on ZT Forums, if you can clarify!
notes: Conversion by The Glass Fractal. See BGG (?) and Tiny Battles Publishing for more information!    Produced with the kind permission of Tiny Battle Publishing & Tom Russell.

title: Stand At Mortain 1.0
description:
Designed by Paul Rorhbaugh.  As arted by Craig Granado!
'Stand at Mortain' is the first game in the Pocket Battle Games series from LPS, Inc. as distributed by ATO Magazine . . .
notes: Conversion by federico67.  An older ZT1 link, and found by R. Peterson! Stand at Mortain is a mini-game complete with map, rules and counters. No need for dice, use your own deck of standard playing cards and your initiative to enjoy this simple-but-exciting WW2 game. See BGG and ATO Magazine for more information!

title: Star Trek Deck Building Game
description: Designer: Alex Bykov, Artist: Jak L. Hueng.  Permission to share the game granted by Alex Bykov.  Permission to use play mats granted by Nersi Nikakhtar
notes: Conversion by btrhoads.  Players take on the role of Captain of a salvaged Starship. They will search for new allies such as Picard, Data, and other famous Characters. They will Explore space to complete Missions, Encounter Events, and meet Starships that could be friend or foe. See BGG and Bandai (Japanese) for more information!

title: Star Trek Fleet Captains - in English
description:
Designed by Mike Elliot, Bryan Kinsella and Ethan Pasternack.  Graphic design (artistry) is unknown; if you know, please leave a message on ZT Forums! 
Awards: 2012 International Gamers Award - General Strategy: Two-players Nominee; 2012 Golden Geek Best 2-Player Board Game Nominee!
ZT Note:  Nice 3-D Minis!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  Take the helm of Federation and Klingon vessels. Use frames and ship cards to keep track of stats (as a substitute for missing click bases).  Flip ships over (double right click) to reveal ship names.   Players must own the game to use this gamebox. See BGG and Wiz Kids for more information! Found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Star Trek Fleet Captains V2.4 - Po Polsku
description:
