Flip ships over (double right click) to reveal ship names.   Players must own the game to use this gamebox. See BGG and Wiz Kids for more information! Found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Starship Troopers
description:
Designed by Randall C. Reed.  As arted by George Goebel, A. Richard Hamblen, Looking Glass Photographics (unusual?), Emily March and Randall C. Reed.  Anyone capable of commenting on Looking Glass Photographics - see ZT Forums!
Game based on R Heinlein novel!
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson.  A faithful conversion of AH's game of tactical Interstellar War.   Starship Troopers is based upon the popular novel of the same name written by the dean of science fiction writers, Robert A. Heinlein. In the novel, Heinlein describes a futuristic war involving homo sapiens from our Earth (Terrans) against a Humanoid race (nicknamed the 'Skinnies' for obvious physical attributes) and their cobelligerents, the totally alien Arachnids. See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information!

title: Steam
description:
Designed by Martin Wallace.  Artwork by John Austin, Jared Blando, Craig Hamilton and Christopher Moeller.
Awards: 7 awards, see BGG entry!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  If you know please leave a message on ZT Forums. Steam-belching iron horses roar across the wild plains! An older ZT1 ZTB as found in the Zwever Collection.  Submitted by R. Peterson. See BGG and Mayfair Games for more information!

title: Sticks & Stones (With New Artwork)
description:
Designed by David Ray.  Originally arted by Pat Hidy.
Microgame #11.
New artwork by Alois Schimmerlos.   This ZTB has both new and original map!
notes: Conversion by E. Sprague. "Sticks & Stones" is a wargame about warfare in the late Stone Age. Each player arms his warriors, as he sees fit, with stone axes, spears, bows, or just bare hands. Please use the 'terrain trowel' to access 'village' artwork! See BGG for more information!

title: Stone Age V2
description:
Designed by Bernd Brunnhofer.  Artwork by Michael Menzel.
Awards:  Over 29 Awards - see BGG entry.
notes: Conversion by tannoiser.  Gather resources, raise animals, and build the tools to start your civilization.  V2 is hi-res vwersion. This an older ZT1 ZTB found in the Zwever Collection. (V1 Available on request - Lo-Res,), V2 - Hi-res) found in Geralt Collection and submitted by R. Peterson. See BGG and Hans im Gluck for more information!

title: Stonewall at Cedar Mountain
description: Designed by Hampton Newsome.  Graphics by Edwin Austin Forbes and Hampton Newsome.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  This is a desk top published game from the mid 1990's - a quick playing brigade level treatment of the Battle of Cedar Mountain that includes chit pull activation and orders mechanisms for movement and combat. See BGG for more information!

title: Stonewall in the Valley
description:
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski
Artwork: Charles Kibler
Mapboard: Kurt Miller
Cover Art: Keith Rocco
Awards & Honors:
  1995 Charles S. Roberts Best Pre-World War II Board Game Nominee
notes: Conversion by Mitch King. Stonewall in the Valley is part of the Great Battles of the Civil War series.  This covers the 1862 Valley Campaign from March through June 1862.  It also includes John Menichelli's 1864 Shenandoah Valley Campaign which is posted on Multi-Man Publishing's GCACW support site.  The game box includes setups for all five 1862 scenarios plus the three 1864 scenarios.  See BGG for more details.  One player must own Avalon Hill's "Stonewall in the Valley" to use this game box.

title: Stonewall Jackson's Way II
description:
Stonewall Jackson's Way II
Copyright© 2013 Multi-Man Publishing
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski, Ed, Beach, Mike Bellles, Chris Withers
Artwork:  Nicolás Eskubi, Charles Kibler
Cover Art: Keith Rocco
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  Stonewall Jackson's Way II is part of the Great Battles of the Civil War series.  This covers the August, 1862 campaign from Cedar Mountain to the 2nd Battle of Bull Run.  The game box includes setups for all nine scenarios.  Note that this game box does not include the 1861 Bull Run campaign.  See BGG and Multi-Man Publishing for more details.  One player must own MMP's Stonewall Jackson's Way II to use this game box.

title: Stonewall Jackson's Way II-1861 Campaign
description:
Stonewall Jackson's Way II-1861
Copyright© 2013 Multi-Man Publishing
Designers: Joseph M. Balkoski, Ed, Beach, Mike Bellles, Chris Withers
Artwork:  Nicolás Eskubi, Charles Kibler
Cover Art: Keith Rocco
ZT Note:  This ZTB is the 1,100th ZTB on our Site!!
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  Stonewall Jackson's Way II is part of the Great Battles of the Civil War series.  This game box covers the July, 1861 campaign in northern Virginia dubbed "All Green Alike" by MMP.  The game box includes setups for all nine scenarios.  See BGG and Multi-Man Publishing for more details.  One player must own MMP's "Stonewall Jackson's Way II" to use this game box.  If you play Scenarios 1, 2 or 7, one player should also own Avalon Hill's "Here Come the Rebels!"

title: Stonewall's Sword: The Battle of Cedar Mountain
description: Designed by Hermann Luttmann.  Originally arted by Richard N. Barber (Map) and Charles J. Kibler II (Counters).
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge. Stonewall's Sword: The Battle of Cedar Mountain is a two-player wargame on The Battle of Cedar Mountain, August 9th, 1862. One player commands Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson's Confederate troops and the other controls Nathaniel Banks' Union troops. See BGG and Revolution Games for further information!

title: Stonne Heights
description:
Designed by Pedro Ramis & Rat Tapio.  Artist's unknown.  Should you know, please advise on ZT Forums.
ZT Folk, if you are an ASL fan, this is a must have!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  Should you know, please advise on ZT Forums.  An old ZT1 design. A new ATS (Advanced Tobruk System) game designed on site by Pedro Ramis, French armor clashes with elite German troops in 1940. Amazing map, unique orders of battle. See Massive Char B1 bis French tanks smash through the gardens of Stonne. See BGG and Crtical Hit for more information!

title: Streets of Stalingrad
description: Designed by Dana Lombardy based on historical research by David Parham. Graphic design by Dana Lombardy.  Awards:  1980 Charles S. Roberts Best Initial Release Nominee and 1980 Charles S. Roberts Best Initial Release Winner!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Setup for combined scenarios 1-3. "Streets of Stalingrad" is a World War 2 East Front wargame that models the fight for the city of Stalingrad, September-October, 1942, at the company level. It employs a scale of 300 meters per hex, with daily turns and 2160 counters. The two designers spent years researching the orders of battle and aerial maps to produce a game that is possibly the most researched and arguably the most accurate depiction of a battle, mechanics aside. See BGG for more information!

title: Strife V1.1 - Po Polsku
description:
Strife - po Polsku
Designed by Christopher Hamm. Artwork by Jonathan Powell. Copyright© 2014 Cube Factory of Ideas Publisher: Cube Factory of Ideas, V3G.
notes: Nawrócenie przez Geralta. Strife, strategiczna gra karciana dla dwóch graczy. Każdy gracz ma tę samą rękę dziesięciu mistrzów i będzie nimi grać jednocześnie, walcząc o kluczowe miejsca warte różne punkty zwycięstwa. Wymyślenie, jak przechytrzyć przeciwnika, to prawdziwe wyzwanie. (Geralt's conversion. Strife, a two-player strategy card game. Each player has the same hand of ten champions and will simultaneously play them as they fight over key locations worth varying victory points. Figuring out how to outmaneuver your opponent is where the true challenge lies.) See BGG for more information! This ZTB was found in the Geralt Collection and submitted by F. Jordan.

title: Strike the Bear
description: Designed by Roger Nord. Graphics by Randy Lein & Brandon Pennington. Copyright© Landsknecht Publishing Services, 2010, Publisher: Against the Odds (ATO), LPS.  By kind permission of Against the Odds Magazine.
notes: Conversion by D. Deitch.  Strike the Bear is one of four simulations of Operation Barbarossa that was published in the 2010 Annual Issue of Against the Odds magazine. The issue was exploring the reasons why the Germans were unable to capture Moscow in 1941.  Strike the Bear was Roger Nord’s contribution. His design underscores the fluidity of the campaign by having territorial objectives change during the course of the game…sometimes even in the middle of a turn. The counters and map are rendered at 600 dpi.  At least one player must own game to download and play. See BGG and ATO & ATO#2 for more information. This ZTB was found in the Against the Odds Magazine's Official Game Aids and the Geralt Collection!

title: Summer of 1863, The
description: Designed by Tom Eskay.  Map artist Todd A. Davis.

title: The Battle of the Japan Sea (日本海大海戦)
description:

notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. In the early 1980s, handheld electronic games were all the rage in Japan, and board games publishers were feeling nervous. The folks at Epoch decided that the best way to combat this threat was to create a line of handheld electronic wargames: the Epoch Wargame Electronics series . In truth, the only thing "electronic" about them was that they used a random number generator in place of a die. And, although technically they could be held by hand, they were still pretty big at about 37.5cm x 24cm x 2.5cm. The board was made of sheet metal, and the pieces were magnetic. The Battle of the Japan Sea (on Tsushima, the decisive naval engagement of the Russo-Japanese War) was the first of twelve releases in the series. The only chart is the "Hit Probability Table" integrated into the "Electronic Results Device". See BGG for more information.

notes: Conversion by S. Rugge.  Boots uses an interactive game turn in which both players command an overall force made up of several sub-commands. During each turn, players alternate picking "command markers," which designate the sub-command within their force they may then use to conduct operations. The player then moves units of that sub-command and, at the completion of its movement, may conduct attacks with the units of that same sub-command. Play then passes to the other player, who similarly picks a marker and moves and fights. That procedure continues until all command markers have been picked. Additionally, certain events cause players to pick "heroism markers" at random, which may generate anything from mad, impetuous charges to abject surrenders. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Troina '43
description: Designed by Brian L. Knipple. Map Graphics by Brian L. Knipple and Stephanie J. Tibbetts. Counter graphics by Jeffry Tibbetts.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Troina '43 simulates the July-August 1943 battle for the town of Troina in northeastern Sicily. The US 1st Infantry Division and the 39th Regiment of the 9th Infantry Division attempted to pierce the German 15th Panzergrenadier Division's line west of the town in an effort to trap the Axis troops that were falling back to the northwestern corner of the island. For more information, see BGG and Just Plain Wargames .

title: Tsushima
description:
Designed by Marc W. Miller.  Arted by Paul Richard Banner (aka Rich Banner).
A companion game with 'Port Arthur.'
The earliest known wargame concerning this historical Battle (February 1904).
notes: Conversion by R. Peterson. Tsushima is a strategic game of the naval war between Russia and Japan, 1904-05. Individual ship counters, searching for the enemy, and when encounters occur, engaging in combat. The first scenario: "The Battle of Port Author" is setup. See BGG and FarFutures for more information!

title: TSWW (The 2nd World War):  Blitzkrieg
description: Designed by John Bannerman.  Artist Unknown.  Should you know, please inform on ZunZtu Forums!

These are supported by a meticulously researched Order of Battle for the first year of the Second World War and include additional details for the United Kingdom and Germany until June 1941:  Blitzkrieg! See BGG and TKC Games for more information!

title: Turning Point: Stalingrad
description:
Designed by Don Greenwood.  As originally arted by Charles J. Kibler II and George Ira Parrish, Jr.
Awards:  1989 Charles S. Roberts Best World War II Board Game Nominee!
notes: Conversion by maxfin (Maaaax).  Turning Point: Stalingrad is mid-complexity wargame on the battle of Stalingrad during World War 2. Attackers from the German 6th Army must dislodge the Russian 62nd Army and take the city of Stalingrad before the commencement of Operation Uranus. If the city could be taken, German troops could then be re-deployed to reinforce the Italian and Rumanian formations holding the flanks of along the Volga. The fiasco at Stalingrad can then be prevented. See BGG and Avalon Hill for further information!

description: Designed by Théophile Monnier & de Nicolas Stratigos.  Artists (all versions): Didier Bourgeois, Christophe Camilotte & Giuseppe Rava.  As first seen in VV # 46.
notes: Conversion by Provence.  Avec l'aimable autorisation de Vae Victis Magazine No 46. Vae Victis issue 46. This game covers the battle of Verdun at the scale of one day per turn, 850 m per hex, and counters of regiments and battallions of infantry (plus counters representing command units, aircraft squadrons, and artillery groups). The game uses a slightly modified and updated version of the system used in Vae Victis issue 24, "Le Matz." It is a relatively simple game, with just over four pages of rules. notes: Conversion by D. Jones. Vicksburg was the key. Holding it meant "holding the South together," with access to all the western men, food, horses, supplies... and Mexican ports. See BGG and TPS for more information!

title: Victory at Midway
description: Designed by Ben Knight.  Artist/Graphics - Unknown; please inform on ZT Forums if known!  Highly acclaimed game, as originally introduced in Command Magazine #14.
notes: Conversion by D. Deitch.  Players take up the roles of the naval commanders and make their plans on their own maps in a "double-blind" turn-based system. Without knowledge of their opponent's fleet position, they move their ships, conduct aerial reconnaissance (calling out hexes and waiting for their opponent's response, as in Battleship), and designate areas for air strikes. The strikes are revealed and resolved before proceeding with other naval engagements (ship-to-ship combat, bombardment and invasion of land targets). Battles are resolved by comparing a die roll to the unit's strength for successful hits instead of referring to charts. See BGG for further information!

The 17x22" map shows the area from Brest to Paris, and from Cherbourg to the Loire River. See BGG for more information!

One player commands the French army withdrawing from Spain under the command of Marshal Jourdan and King Joseph, while the other player leads the Anti-French (referred to as “Anglo-Allied”) forces consisting of the combined British, Portuguese and Spanish army under General Sir Arthur Wellesley, Viscount of Wellington." notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.   Setup provided.  Players play tactical battles in Salerno 1943, at the the platon and company scale. Charts in English and Japanese. I took the English charts from the translation available at ConSimWorld Forum . See BGG for more information.

title: Wacht Am Rhein': The Battle of the Bulge BIS
description:
Designed by Joseph M. Balkoski, James F. Dunnigan and Redmond Aksel Simonsen.  As originally arted by Redmond Aksel Simonsen.
Awards: 1977 Charles S. Roberts Best Tactical Nominee
notes: Conversion by D.Davis (Dan Davis) Campaign Game is set up. Wacht Am Rhein': The Battle of the Bulge. 16 Dec '44 - 2 Jan '45. SPI's monster game of the Battle of the Bulge. 4 maps. This is a grand tactical simulation of the Battle of the Bulge. Recreate the decisive engagement that represented Hitler's last major effort to win the Second World War. Not a simple game to learn, but once mastered a very enjoyable game. NOTE:  Added German companies (on the "tried units"countersheet).  Have not fixed the reversed positions of the XLVII and LVIII Corps troops. (superceedes 1st version). See BGG and Decision Games for more information!

One on four games included in the Napoleon At War QuadriGame. The games in this set are based on the Napoleon At Waterloo system which is a basic movement-combat system with hard zones of control. See BGG and DG for more information!

title: Walcheren 1809

description: Designed by Robert J. Beyma and Frank Davis.  Graphics by the prolific artists Rodger B. MacGowan and Dale A. Sheaffer.

Each historical scenario is presented as a separate 2-player game with an average playing time of 2-3 hours. See BGG and Avalon Hill for more information.

title: WAR AT SEA PLUS+, as it should have been!

Designed by John Edwards. Artists: John Edwards, Art Lupinacci, W. Scott Moores and Robert D. Watts. A Jedko Game, re-imagined by Avalon Hill.

Please leverage ZT's User-interface and select the various scenarios!!!!!!! See BGG and Avalon Hill for further information.

title: Waterloo 1st Ed. PLUS+
description: WaterlooZT PLUS; Design by Charles Roberts and Thomas Shaw; Napoleon's last campaign culminating in his epic defeat at Waterloo.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. This is Avalon Hill's 1962 edition of Napoleon's campaign against the Prussian and Anglo Allied armies. This gamebox features the original artwork cleaned up to remove the river, woods, and hilltop ambiguities while maintaining the nostalgia of a sixty-two year old classic. The counter sheet has been reworked so each playing piece is perfectly "die cut" on center. CRTs are offered as moveable cards in three sizes and the Turn Record and Reinforcement Track is located on the main screen for easy access. Scenarios include an Open and a Sample French and Prussian starting setup. And because this is a Plus box, the rules are included. Here they are conveniently available on tabs. With Napoleon’s escape from exile and return to France, his Grande Armee is once again on the march. Can the Anglo-Allied forces under Wellington and the Prussian army under Blücher stop him?" title: Waterloo 2nd Edition PLUS+ with Tournament Scenario
description: Waterloo PLUS+ w Tournament; Design by Charles Roberts and Thomas Shaw; Napoleon's last campaign culminating in his epic defeat at Waterloo. This gamebox has the redrawn map checked for tournament play by Waterloo Gamemaster Ed Menzel and includes 2nd edition and Tournament rules. Avalon Hill 1962
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. This is Avalon Hill's 1962 edition of Napoleon's campaign against the Prussian and Anglo Allied armies. Scenarios are included for both the standard game and Tournament competition. This gamebox features the original artwork cleaned up to remove the river, woods, and hilltop ambiguities while maintaining the nostalgia of a sixty-two year old classic. The map corrections were made under the direction of Ed Menzel, Gamemaster of the Waterloo Tournaments. (Tournament information included.) The counters have been colored slightly to mimic the basic uniforms at Waterloo: The French are blue over white and the British, red over gray. (Prussians are green over gray in keeping with Avalon Hill's original choice.) The little added color really pops but for traditionalists, the 1962 counter art is available on the flip side. CRTs are offered as two-sided, moveable cards in three sizes and the Turn Record and Reinforcement Track is located on the main screen for easy access. The Tournament scenario uses a 10 sided die and matching CRT. 2nd Edition rules are included as tabs and three pages of Tournament rules are added in that scenario. An additional page of ZunTzu notes shows some tips for new ZunTzu players. For more information see BGG , Waterloo Tournament , Email Tournament , and WBC

title: West Wall Quad
description:
Designer: Kip Allen
Artists: Redmond Simonsen
Updated Maps: Steven Oliver (Arnhem), Robin LeBon (Huertgen & Bastogne)
notes: Conversion by Mitch King.  The Westwall Quad feaures four battles in Western Europe in 1944-45.  The first is Arnhem, featuring Montgomery's Operation Market-Garden in September, 1994.  The second features the intense, close-in combat in the Huertgen Forest in the fall of 1944.  The third features the defense and relief of Bastogne during the Battle of the Bulge in December, 1994.  The final battle covers the Allies first crossing of the Rhine River when they unexpectedly capture the Ludendorf Bridge before German engineers could blow it up.  Setups are included for all four games.  These are "beer and pretzels" games suitable for an evening of play.  See BGG and Decision Games ( DG ) for more information.  One of the players in the game MUST own a physical copy of SPI's "Westwall Quad" to use this game box.

notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Combines the maps and counters for all 13 games and expansions in the Wrzesień 1939 series published by Heksagon and Taktyka i Strategia between 2003 and 2015: Bzura 1939, Góry Świętokrzyskie, Kock 1939, Lądowa Obrona Wybrzeża 1939 (a.k.a. Gdańsk 1939), Linia Wisły, Mława 1939, Piotrków 1939, Pomorze 1939, Przemyśla 1939, San 1939, Śląsk 1939, Suwalszczyzna 1939, and Wielkopolska 1939. All games designed by Wojciech Zalewski. See BGG for more information (in English)!

title: Wrzesień 1939 v1.1 - Po Polsku
description:
Projekt i wykonanie Wojciech Zalewski. Jak napisano przez wiele Nieznanych osób. Jeśli wiesz, skontaktuj się na forach ZT (w języku polskim lub angielskim). Oryginalna polska gra(y)! Ta wersja ma polskie CRT itp.
Update Note: Works best in ZT1.4.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Łączy mapy i liczniki dla wszystkich 13 gier i rozszerzeń z serii Wrzesień 1939 wydanych przez Heksagon i Taktyka i Strategia w latach 2003-2015: Bzura 1939, Góry Świętokrzyskie, Kock 1939, Lądowa Obrona Wybrzeża 1939 (ps. Gdańsk 1939), Linia Wisły, Mława 1939, Piotrków 1939, Pomorze 1939, Przemyśla 1939, San 1939, Śląsk 1939, Suwalszczyzna 1939,  i Wielkopolska 1939. Wszystkie gry zaprojektowane przez Wojciecha Zalewskiego. Zobacz BGG , aby uzyskać więcej informacji!

title: Wurzburg: Soviet-American Combat in the '70's
description:
Designed by the famous James F. Dunnigan.  An early piece of artwork by the famous Redmond Askel Simonsen!
This version does have some new counter artwork by an unknown artist!
Awards:  Produced in 2005 by the Brazilian Education group:  a group dedicated to spreading wargames in South America!
notes: Conversion by Luiz Cláudio. Part of the Modern Battles: Four Contemporary Conflicts quadrigames which included standard rules for each game as well as exclusive rules for each game in the series. Wurzburg covers a hypothetical conflict between the US and Russia near the German city of Wurzburg. See BGG and DG (Decision Games) for more information!

title: WW2 Deluxe
description:
Designed by Jon Compton.  Arted by Jon Compton, Ilya Kudriashov and Wojciech Zalewski.
A Polish company - rules will be needed to play!
notes: Conversion by Maaaax. WW2 Deluxe is a grand-strategic game, for two, utilizing armies or army groups, air forces, and fleets. The game covers the entire conflict in Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. The War in Europe 1939-1945. Campaign Game + 6 smaller scenarios. See BGG and Canvas Temple for more information!

title: Yggdrasil
description:
Designed by Cédric Lefebvre and Fabrice Rabellino.  Graphics by Pierô.
We are unsure of the publisher or edition - please leave a message on ZT Forums, if you know!
notes: Conversion by Geralt.  Yggdrasil is a co-operative game in which players are different gods of the Norse mythology: Odin, Thor, Tyr, Frey, Heimdall and Freyja. Monsters, the wolf Fenrir, the huge serpent Jormungand, the Fire Giant Surt, the Goddess of the Dead Hel, the traitor Loki and the cosmic dragon Nidhögg are moving forward in Asgard inescapably and announce the impending coming of chaos and destruction on the world-tree Yggdrasil. Together the players have to resist to the impending coming of the Evil forces in Asgard, the gods' world. See BGG and Z-Man Games for more information!

title: YINSH
description:
Designed by Kris Burm.  Artwork by Kris Burm and Lu'cifer.
One of the Project GIPF set of abstract games.  Awards: Multi-awards winner - see BGG entry for full listing!
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  If you know, please leave a mesage on ZT Forums.  In YINSH, the players each start with five rings on the board . . .The first player to remove three of his rings wins the game. See BGG , Project GIPF and Rio Grande Games for more information! An older ZT1 ZTB as found in the Zwever and Geralt Collections. Submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Yom Kippur PLUS+
description:
Designed by Dean N. Essig and Al Sandrick.  Artists: Dean N. Essig and Shawsun Yamagushi

Awards: 1995 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-World War II Board Game Winner & 1995 Charles S. Roberts Best Post-World War II Board Game Nominee
notes: Conversion by Maaaax.  The Battle for the Sinai, 1973. See BGG snd MMP/Gamers for more information!

title: Yorktown, Battle of
description:
Designed and arted by Steve Kling, who founded The Historical Game Company, LLC in 2014. 
By kind permission of THGC and Mr. Kling.
notes: Conversion by S. Rugge. Battle of Yorktown Sep-Oct, 1781, is a low to moderate complexity tactical wargame covering the Franco-American attack and siege of Yorktown during the American Revolutionary War. One player commands the British and their Hessian mercenaries and the other player commands the Franco-American forces. The game takes about 90 minutes to play! See BGG , Blue Panther and THGC Publishing for more information!

title: You're Bluffing!
description:
Designed by Rudiger-Koltze.  All artists: Bernard Bittler, Josef Blaumeiser and Trevor Dunton.
Awards:  1996 Fairplay À la carte Runner-up and 1985 Spiel des Jahres Recommended!
notes: Conversion by Zwever. Classic bidding and bluffing game. The deck consists of sets of farm animals, 4 cards per animal. Players auction off the top animal of the deck, or try to complete their set by trading with another player. Highest bid wins, but auctioneer always has the choice to buy the animal for the same price as the highest bid. Trading is a blind bidding system: both players place their bid face down on the table and reveal them simultaneously to each other. High bidder gets the other player's animal. Both players swap their bid. It's best to bid just a little bit more than your opponent, but just how much did he bid? See BGG for more information!  Originally on ZT1! From the Zwever Collection

title: Yugen PLUS+
description: Yugen PLUS; Design and Art by Stefan Karamanov; PNP edition.
notes: Conversion by Frank Jordan. Yugen is an abstract strategy game for two players. Tiles are placed on a diagonal board with the objective of getting two of three "philosophers" to come across your border. The tiles represent the forces of Earth, Air, Fire, and Water and their interaction can either pull or push the philosophers along. The rules take up only three pages (with large illustrations) and they are available on tabs for easy reference during play. Two additional pages of ZunTzu notes are included to show new players how ZunTzu handles tiles (like cards) and how they can be manipulated and kept hidden in your hand. See BGG & Yugen platyest site for more information!

title: Yukimura Gaiden (幸村外伝)
description: Designed by Makoto Fukuda. Its original Tsukuda release in 1986 was the first game in the Sengoku Gassen series. The version used for this gamebox was published by Game Journal in 2016 as Separate Issue #7.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. The summer 1615 siege of Osaka marked the final triumph of the Tokugawa clan over the Toyotomi clan, determining the destiny of Japan for the next 250 years. This game is based on the Battle of Tennoji, the climax of that campaign. Charts in English and Japanese. Setup provided. See BGG for more information. The ZunTzu gamebox can be downloaded from the Game Journal Website , as can an English translation of the rules and charts .

links.title: English translation of the rules and charts

title: Yukimura Gaiden Episode 0 (幸村外伝 Episode-0)
description: Designed by Asano Ryūji. Published in Game Journal #71. Based on the Yukimura Gaiden game system (formerly known as Sengoku Gassen).
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. More action from the summer campaign of the siege of Osaka in 1615, this time the battles of Domyoji and Yao-Wakae. Charts in English and Japanese (note that the English-language charts on the map are terrain pieces that can be removed to reveal the original Japanese versions). Setups provided for both battles (in one scenario). See BGG for more information. The ZunTzu gamebox can be downloaded from the Game Journal Website , as can an English translation of the rules and charts .

links.title: English translation of the rules and charts

title: Zaibatsu
description: Design and artistry by Froylan Rutiaga.
notes: Conversion by Unknown.  Should you know, please leave a message on ZT Forums!  The game is set in a cyberpunk future, players represent supercorporations rivals, the Zaibatsu, who struggle to obtain the domain and control of the global network of information, Cybernet and for this we serve a large number of agents, mercenaries pawns they use to achieve their targets. See BGG & Zaibatsu site for more information! This older ZT1 ZTB was found in both the Geralt and Zwever Collections; submitted by R. Peterson.

title: Zargo's Lords 1ere Ed
description: Designed by Marco Donadoni.  Graphics by Enea Riboldi.
notes: Conversion by Provence.  Avec l'aimable autorisation de Mr Marco Donadoni.  By kind permission of Mr. Marco Donadoni. The first fantasy wargame ever published in Italy. A big success in the '80s, a game who introduced a lot of people in the hobby. See BGG and International Team for more information!

title: Zorndorf
description:
Designed by Paul Dangel. Counter graphics by Paul Dangel. Map graphics by Rick Barber.
Award:  1996 Charles S. Roberts Best Wargaming Graphics Nominee
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Zorndorf is the second game in the acclaimed Battles from the Age of Reason (BAR) series. The system presents a detailed simulation of warfare in the age of linear tactics. It is the framework through which players maneuver historic armies while seeking to discover which combinations of units and formations lead to victory, or are a formula for defeat. I have added markers to make it possible to use the casualty rosters on the screen. Includes setup for the Grand Battle scenario. See BGG & COA (Clash of Arms) for more information.

title: Zulu Attack
description: Designed by Fred Chatham and David Ferguson. Graphics by Fred Chatham.
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon.  "Zulu Attack" recreates the battle of Isandlawana, which took place 22 Jan 1879 in the opening exchanges of the Anglo-Zulu war. See BGG & Grognard for more information.

title: Zulu Attack!  Isandlwana January 22, 1879
description: Designed by Fred Chatham and David Ferguson. As arted by George Ira Parrish, Jr.
notes: Conversion by R Peterson.  Historically, the British forces lost.  Can you defeat the hordes of Zulu Warriors?  An epic battle of rifle vs spear. See BGG for more information including errata!

title: Zulu: Isandhlwana
description:
Designed by Daryl Shirley. Art and graphics by James Mirick and Ron Reynolds.
An early and rare game on this subject - in the 70's or now!
See an another1970's game "
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. "January 22, 1879: Isandhlwana, Zululand. British Army Destroyed!"  A dramatic game of one of histories great victories of the Zulu! See BGG for more information.

title: Zulu: Naka
description:
Designed by Daryl Shirley and John Lewis. Art and graphics by James Mirick and Ron Reynolds.
A must see for 'Shaka' fans!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. A little represented War; those between the Army of Shaka Zulu and the opposing tribes that the emerging Zulu army-machine, fought and defeated! The counters represent the on the war to the short lived Zulu empire. See BGG for more information.

title: Zulu: Rorkes' Drift
description:
Designed by Daryl Shirley. Art and graphics by James Mirick and Ron Reynolds.
An early and rare game on this subject - in the 70's or now!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. Download this game, to remeber a small success (?) of British colonial arms. Fought on January 23, 1879, the 'Battle of Rorke's Drift' could well be called the battle of the 'Victoria Cross.' Of the one hundred thirty personnel involved in the defense of the station and hospital at the Drift, eight of them received this most coveted of all British decorations . . . (Victoria Cross)." Also download Zulu: Isandhlwana on this site . . . See BGG for more information.

title: Zulu: Ulundi
description:
Designed by Daryl Shirley and John Lewis. Art and Graphics by James Mirick and Ron Reynolds.
A rare game of a decisive victory!
notes: Conversion by T. Gordon. In July 1879, clouds of white and grey smoke rose over the battle field of Ulundi: the massed crash of British Imperial infantry rifle fire was decimating the ranks of Zulu the Army of twenty thousand warriors. Wave after wave of Zulu might flowed against the bulwark of Briish Colonial infantry, only to be drive back by the combined forces of rifle, machine gun and artillery fire.  Can you do better? See BGG for more information.

title: Zürich 1799
description: Designed by Frédéric Bey and Pascal da Silva.  As arted by Didier Bourgeois, Christophe Camilotte and Giuseppe Rava.  As first seen in VV Magazine No. 29.
notes: Conversion by L. Gary. This game is the third in the "Jours de Gloire" battle series, which uses a modified version of the rules for GMT's "Glory" games by Richard H Berg. These rules were later adapted by GMT for their "Triumph and Glory" game. This game covers Masséna's great victory at the battle of Zurich in 1799. See BGG and Vae Victis Magazine for further information!
